1. In **Settings → Features**, turn on **MCP server**. Its card shows the **Endpoint**, `https://cms.example.com/mcp`, on the same host as the content API.
2. In **Settings → API tokens**, choose **Create token**. Pick **Read-only** unless the agent should write, or **Custom** to allow only some types and actions. Copy the token: it is shown once. See [API tokens](/verdin/guides/auth/api-tokens/).
3. Connect your client with the endpoint and the token (below).

## Connect a client

[Section titled “Connect a client”](#connect-a-client)

The server speaks MCP’s Streamable HTTP transport. Every client needs the URL and an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.

* Claude Code

  The **MCP server** card has this command under **Add it to Claude Code** (**Copy the command**); replace `<token>` with your API token:

  Terminal

  ```sh
  claude mcp add --transport http verdin https://cms.example.com/mcp \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
  ```

* Cursor

  .cursor/mcp.json

  ```json
  {
    "mcpServers": {
      "verdin": {
        "url": "https://cms.example.com/mcp",
        "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <token>" }
      }
    }
  }
  ```

* VS Code

  .vscode/mcp.json

  ```json
  {
    "servers": {
      "verdin": {
        "type": "http",
        "url": "https://cms.example.com/mcp",
        "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <token>" }
      }
    }
  }
  ```

* Claude Desktop

  Claude Desktop’s configuration file starts local servers, so bridge to the HTTP endpoint with [`mcp-remote`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote):

  claude_desktop_config.json

  ```json
  {
    "mcpServers": {
      "verdin": {
        "command": "npx",
        "args": ["mcp-remote", "https://cms.example.com/mcp", "--header", "Authorization: Bearer ${VERDIN_TOKEN}"],
        "env": { "VERDIN_TOKEN": "<token>" }
      }
    }
  }
  ```

Client configuration formats change; check your client’s documentation if a key is not recognized. Then ask the agent something like *“List the articles published this week in the News category”*.

## Tools

[Section titled “Tools”](#tools)

| Tool                               | Needs               | What it does                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `list_content_types`               | `find` or `findOne` | The content types the caller can read, with their kind and attributes.                                                                                                 |
| `get_content_type`                 | `find` or `findOne` | A content type’s attributes: types, options and relations.                                                                                                             |
| `find_entries`                     | `find`              | Entries of a type. `query` takes the REST API’s parameters as JSON (`filters`, `sort`, `fields`, `populate`, `pagination`); `status: "draft"` also needs `readDrafts`. |
| `get_entry`                        | `findOne`           | One entry by `documentId` (single types: without it).                                                                                                                  |
| `create_entry`                     | `create`            | Creates an entry from `data`, as in the REST API. `status: "draft"` saves a draft.                                                                                     |
| `update_entry`                     | `update`            | Updates an entry (single types: without `documentId`).                                                                                                                 |
| `delete_entry`                     | `delete`            | Deletes an entry.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `publish_entry`, `unpublish_entry` | `publish`           | Publishes or unpublishes an entry.                                                                                                                                     |

Tools take `uid` (such as `api::article`) and, for localized types, `locale`. Each tool checks the same permission as the matching REST route, and writes go through the same path as the REST API: validation, plugin hooks, review stages, webhooks, content history and audit logs. An agent can do nothing its token cannot do over REST.

See [Permissions](/verdin/reference/permissions/) for the content API actions.

## Authentication

[Section titled “Authentication”](#authentication)

The endpoint takes the same credentials as the content API:

* an API token, the usual choice for agents;
* an end user’s JWT, for an agent acting as a signed-in user of your app;
* no `Authorization` header, for the public role’s permissions.

An invalid token answers `401`. The server keeps no sessions and opens no streams: each request is a JSON-RPC `POST` answered with JSON (`GET` answers `405`).

### Browser origins

[Section titled “Browser origins”](#browser-origins)

Requests that carry an `Origin` header, which browsers send, are refused unless the origin is listed under **Allowed browser origins** on the **MCP server** card. This protects against DNS rebinding, where a web page tricks the browser into calling a server on your network. Command-line and desktop clients send no `Origin`, so the list is usually empty.

Caution

An agent with a full-access token can delete and publish content. Give agents read-only or custom tokens scoped to what they need. For drafts an agent writes, a [review workflow](/verdin/guides/content/review-workflows/) keeps a person between the agent and publishing.

To give editors AI help inside the admin panel instead (translation, alt text, SEO suggestions), see [AI actions](/verdin/guides/integrations/ai-actions/).

# Webhooks

> Call your own endpoints when content or media changes, check that deliveries come from Verdin, and handle retries.

Webhooks send an HTTP `POST` to a URL of yours when content or media changes: rebuild a static site, purge a cache, sync a search index, post to a chat. Deliveries are queued, signed, retried and logged.

This page walks through setting one up and receiving it. The events, payloads and headers are listed in the [webhooks reference](/verdin/api/webhooks/).

## Turn it on

[Section titled “Turn it on”](#turn-it-on)

The **Webhooks** feature is on by default; you can switch it off in **Settings → Features**. Managing webhooks needs the **Manage webhooks** permission (`webhooks.manage`). See [Permissions](/verdin/reference/permissions/).

## Create a webhook

[Section titled “Create a webhook”](#create-a-webhook)

1. Go to **Settings → Webhooks** and choose **New webhook**.
2. Under **General**, give it a **Name** and the **URL** Verdin should call.
3. Under **Events**, pick the events that trigger a delivery: **Entries** (create, update, publish, unpublish, discard draft, delete), **Media**, **Releases** (**Release published**) and **Review workflows** (**Entry stage changed**).
4. Under **Content types**, keep **All content types** or pick some. This only filters entry events; media events are sent regardless.
5. Under **Headers**, add any headers your endpoint needs, such as an `authorization` token (**Add header**). `content-type`, `host` and the `x-verdin-*` headers are set by Verdin.
6. Under **Signing**, keep **Sign deliveries** on (the default).
7. Choose **Create**. Verdin shows the signing secret (`whsec_…`) once: copy it into your endpoint’s configuration.

**Enabled** switches a webhook off without deleting it. Disabled webhooks receive no events but can still be tested.

## Test it

[Section titled “Test it”](#test-it)

Choose **Send test event** on the webhook. Verdin sends, right away:

```json
{ "event": "trigger-test", "createdAt": "2026-09-25T09:00:00.000Z" }
```

The delivery appears in the webhook’s **Delivery log** with its status, HTTP status, duration and the start of the response body. Open a delivery for the full payload and the error, if any.

To receive webhooks on your machine while you develop, run the server with `verdin dev`: it allows `localhost` URLs, which `verdin start` refuses (see [Security](#security)).

## Receive a delivery

[Section titled “Receive a delivery”](#receive-a-delivery)

A delivery is a `POST` with a JSON body and these headers:

| Header               | Value                                                                           |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `content-type`       | `application/json`                                                              |
| `x-verdin-event`     | The event name, such as `entry.publish`.                                        |
| `x-verdin-delivery`  | The delivery id. It stays the same across retries: use it to ignore duplicates. |
| `x-verdin-signature` | `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>`, on signed webhooks.                                |

```json
{
  "event": "entry.publish",
  "createdAt": "2026-09-25T09:00:00.000Z",
  "model": "article",
  "uid": "api::article",
  "entry": { "id": 3, "documentId": "01J…", "title": "Hello", "publishedAt": "2026-09-25T09:00:00.000Z" }
}
```

Answer with any `2xx` status, quickly. Do slow work (a full rebuild) after answering, or queue it: a delivery that takes longer than the timeout (10 seconds by default) counts as failed.

### Verify the signature

[Section titled “Verify the signature”](#verify-the-signature)

`v1` is the HMAC-SHA256 of `"<t>.<raw body>"`, keyed with the webhook’s secret. To check a delivery:

1. Recompute the HMAC over the **raw** request body, not over re-serialized JSON.
2. Compare it with `v1` in constant time.
3. Reject timestamps older than a few minutes, so a captured delivery cannot be replayed.

* Node.js

  ```js
  import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto';


  export function verify(secret, header, rawBody, toleranceSeconds = 300) {
    const { t, v1 } = Object.fromEntries(header.split(',').map((part) => part.split('=')));
    if (Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(t)) > toleranceSeconds) return false;
    const expected = createHmac('sha256', secret).update(`${t}.${rawBody}`).digest('hex');
    return v1?.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(expected), Buffer.from(v1));
  }
  ```

  With Express, keep the raw body: `app.post('/hooks/verdin', express.raw({ type: 'application/json' }), …)` and pass `req.body.toString()`.

* Python

  ```python
  import hashlib, hmac, time


  def verify(secret: str, header: str, raw_body: bytes, tolerance: int = 300) -> bool:
      parts = dict(part.split("=", 1) for part in header.split(","))
      if abs(time.time() - int(parts["t"])) > tolerance:
          return False
      expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), f"{parts['t']}.".encode() + raw_body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
      return hmac.compare_digest(expected, parts["v1"])
  ```

* Edge (Web Crypto)

  ```ts
  export async function verify(secret: string, header: string, rawBody: string, tolerance = 300) {
    const { t, v1 } = Object.fromEntries(header.split(',').map((part) => part.split('=')));
    if (Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(t)) > tolerance) return false;
    const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', new TextEncoder().encode(secret),
      { name: 'HMAC', hash: 'SHA-256' }, false, ['verify']);
    const signature = new Uint8Array(v1.match(/../g)!.map((byte) => parseInt(byte, 16)));
    return crypto.subtle.verify('HMAC', key, signature, new TextEncoder().encode(`${t}.${rawBody}`));
  }
  ```

  `crypto.subtle.verify` compares in constant time.

**Rotate secret** issues a new secret (shown once); the old one stops working at once. **Stop signing** deletes the secret and sends deliveries unsigned.

## Retries

[Section titled “Retries”](#retries)

Deliveries are stored in the database when the change commits and sent by a background worker, so a slow endpoint never slows down editors.

* **Success:** any `2xx` answer.
* **Failure:** anything else, including redirects (they are not followed), connection errors and timeouts.
* **Retries:** a failed delivery is retried after 30 seconds, 2 minutes, 10 minutes, 1 hour and 6 hours. After that it is marked **Failed**.

Choose **Retry** on a delivery in the log to send it again now. The log is kept for 30 days. Since retries reuse the same `x-verdin-delivery`, make your handler idempotent: store the ids you processed, or make the work safe to repeat.

## Security

[Section titled “Security”](#security)

With `verdin start`, webhook URLs may not point at loopback, private, link-local or other reserved addresses, including host names that resolve to one. This keeps an admin from using webhooks to reach internal services (SSRF). Credentials in the URL (`https://user:pass@…`) are refused; send them in a header instead.

verdin.toml

```toml
[webhooks]
allow_private_networks = false   # unset: false with `verdin start`, true with `verdin dev`
timeout_secs = 10
retention_days = 30
```

See [`[webhooks]`](/verdin/reference/configuration/).

## Coming from Strapi

[Section titled “Coming from Strapi”](#coming-from-strapi)

Verdin’s webhooks follow Strapi’s events and payloads, with these differences:

* deliveries are signed, retried and logged;
* a webhook can be limited to some content types;
* Strapi’s `entry.draft-discard` is called `entry.discard-draft`.

To rebuild a static site from the admin with a button instead of on every change, see [Deploys and CDN](/verdin/guides/integrations/deploys-and-cdn/).

# Admin panel

> How Verdin's Angular admin panel is structured, how it builds forms and lists from the schema, and how it is built, embedded in the binary and translated.

This page is for contributors to the admin panel in `admin/`: how the Angular app is organised, how it turns the content schema into forms and lists, and how it ends up inside the `verdin` binary. How to use the panel is covered in the guides; how the server side of the admin API works is in the [admin API reference](/verdin/api/admin/).

The panel is an Angular 22 single-page app: standalone components, zoneless change detection, signals, lazy-loaded routes, and spartan/ui components on Tailwind CSS v4.

## Structure

[Section titled “Structure”](#structure)

```text
admin/
├── src/app/
│   ├── app.config.ts     # providers: router, HttpClient interceptors, Transloco, icons
│   ├── app.routes.ts     # lazy routes, guards (auth, permissions, unsaved changes)
│   ├── core/             # services and pure models: api, auth, schema, i18n, permissions…
│   ├── layout/           # the shell (sidebar, header), home, deploy button
│   ├── features/
│   │   ├── auth/         # login, first admin, invitations, password reset
│   │   ├── dashboard/    # home widgets
│   │   ├── content/      # lists, the entry editor, history, releases, review, import
│   │   │   ├── fields/   # schema-driven form controls and the form model
│   │   │   └── collab/   # comments and tasks
│   │   ├── builder/      # content-type builder (verdin dev only)
│   │   ├── media/        # media library
│   │   ├── releases/
│   │   ├── profile/      # own account, two-factor, passkeys, sessions
│   │   └── settings/     # users, roles, tokens, webhooks, locales, plugins, site features…
│   └── shared/
│       ├── ui/           # spartan helm components, owned by the project
│       └── components/   # app-level shared components (confirm dialog, page header…)
├── public/i18n/          # translation catalogs, one JSON file per language
├── scripts/check-i18n.mjs
└── e2e/                  # Playwright tests and the server they run against
```

**State** lives in signals inside injectable services in `core/` (`Auth`, `Schema`, `I18n`, `Theme`…). There is no store library.

**API access** goes through `core/api.ts`, a small promise-based wrapper over Angular’s `HttpClient`, with hand-written types in `core/types.ts`. The runtime configuration (admin path, API prefix, mode, branding) comes from a `<meta name="verdin-config">` tag the server injects.

**Session.** The access token lives only in memory; the refresh token is an `HttpOnly` cookie scoped to the auth routes. An HTTP interceptor adds the bearer token and, on a `401`, refreshes once and retries; if the refresh fails it sends the user to the login page. Refresh and logout requests carry the `X-Verdin-CSRF` header the server requires. Guards restore the session from the cookie on page load. A `403` that says the role requires two-factor authentication sends the user to set it up.

## Schema-driven forms

[Section titled “Schema-driven forms”](#schema-driven-forms)

The entry editor (`features/content/edit.ts`) has no per-type code. It reads the content types and components from `GET /admin/api/content-types` and `GET /admin/api/components`, and the editor layout from the edit-view settings, and builds the form at runtime with **Signal Forms** (`@angular/forms/signals`):

* The document model is a signal of a plain object (`FormModel` in `fields/model.ts`); the field tree and its validators are derived from the schema.
* A recursive `vd-fields` component (`fields/fields.ts`) renders any attribute map against a field tree. Text, dates and times use native inputs bound with `[formField]`. Custom `FormValueControl`s handle numbers (nullable; big integers stay strings), switches, enumerations, datetimes (local time in the input, UTC in the model), JSON, Markdown, `blocks` (TipTap), media, relations (search-as-you-type picker with ordering) and polymorphic relations.
* Components are nested fieldsets; repeatable components and dynamic zones are reorderable lists. Plugins can register custom field types, rendered as custom elements.
* `toModel` converts a populated document into the form model (relations become `documentId`s, files become ids), and `toPayload` converts back into the `data` payload: empty strings become `null`, render keys (`__key`) and read-only sides (`mappedBy`, `morphOne`, `morphMany`) are dropped. Both are unit tested in `fields/model.spec.ts`.
* Validation derived from the schema gives instant feedback. Conditional fields (`conditions.visible`) are evaluated in the browser by a port of the server’s JSON Logic evaluator (`core/logic.ts`). Cross-field validation rules are checked by the server only. The server stays the authority: its `details.errors[].path` entries are mapped back onto the matching field.
* Saving is explicit, with dirty tracking and a leave-page warning (a route guard plus `beforeunload`). **Publish**, **Unpublish** and **Discard** buttons appear depending on the document’s state. The admin saves drafts only; publishing is always a separate action.

The layout of the editor (field order, widths, labels, descriptions, read-only fields, the field that names related entries) is shared by every admin and stored on the server in `vd_settings`, changed from the **Configure the view** page with the `views.manage` permission.

## Lists

[Section titled “Lists”](#lists)

Content lists (`features/content/list.ts`) use the spartan helm table with server-side pagination, sorting and filters. Filters, search (`_q`) and the page are mirrored in the URL, so a filtered list is a shareable link. Each admin picks the visible columns, default sort and page size per type (`list-view.ts`); those choices are saved in their own preferences on the server, so they follow them across browsers. Lists also update live from the admin event stream.

## Content-type builder

[Section titled “Content-type builder”](#content-type-builder)

The **Content-type builder** is visible only when the server runs in development mode (`verdin dev`) and the admin has `schema.manage`. It edits content types and components in their file format: fields, relation kinds and targets (creating the inverse attribute on the target), components, dynamic zones, lengths, ranges, and the `required`, `unique` and `private` flags.

Every change is first sent to `POST /admin/api/schema/plan`, which validates the would-be schema and returns the migration steps with their risk, their SQL and rename suggestions the user can accept. Confirming calls `POST /admin/api/schema/apply` with the accepted risk level and renames. The server migrates, writes `schema/*.json`, and swaps the running app for the new schema without a restart. See [migration engine](/verdin/internals/migrations/) for what happens on the server.

## Build and distribution

[Section titled “Build and distribution”](#build-and-distribution)

* `ng build` writes the production build to `admin/dist/admin/browser`, with `<base href="/admin/">`.
* The server embeds that folder with `rust-embed` when compiled with the `embed-admin` feature, which release builds and the Docker image use. Without the feature, or when `[admin].assets_dir` is set, it serves the files from disk. `assets_dir` wins over the embedded build.
* The server rewrites `<base href>` to `[admin].path` and injects the runtime configuration as a `<meta>` tag, not an inline script. Changing `admin.path` never requires rebuilding the panel.
* Unknown paths without a file extension fall back to `index.html` for client-side routing. Fingerprinted bundles (`main-ABC123.js`) are cached as `immutable` for a year; everything else is `no-cache`.
* Every admin response carries a strict Content Security Policy (`script-src 'self'`, `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `base-uri 'self'`…), `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`. Angular’s critical-CSS inlining is turned off in `angular.json` because it relies on inline event handlers that the policy forbids.

For frontend work, run the server, then `npm start` in `admin/`: `ng serve` proxies `/admin/api` and `/api` to `http://localhost:1337` (`admin/proxy.conf.json`).

## Translations

[Section titled “Translations”](#translations)

The panel is translated at runtime with Transloco, not with Angular’s compile-time i18n, so one build serves every language and users can switch without a reload.

* Catalogs are flat JSON files in `admin/public/i18n/` (`en.json` is the source), loaded on demand.
* Messages use ICU MessageFormat (`{name}`, `{count, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}}`), interpreted by FormatJS (`intl-messageformat`) through a custom Transloco transpiler. FormatJS interprets messages instead of compiling them to functions, so the CSP needs no `unsafe-eval`.
* Message keys are typed from `en.json` (`core/i18n/keys.ts`): using a key that does not exist is a compile error.
* `npm run i18n:check` checks every catalog against `en.json`: same keys, valid ICU syntax, the same arguments, and every plural category of the language. CI runs it.
* The `I18n` service also provides locale-aware formatting and the first day of the week, taken from the browser’s regional settings with a per-user override.

How to add or update a language is in [translating](/verdin/project/translating/).

# Database layer

> How Verdin talks to PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite through one connection type, a Flavor enum and its own SQL builders, and how it handles each dialect's differences.

This page explains how Verdin supports four database engines with one code path: the `verdin-db` crate that connects and executes, the SQL builders that branch on the engine, and the dialect differences they handle. Read it before you write SQL anywhere in the server. How tables are laid out is in [storage](/verdin/internals/storage/).

## Minimum versions

[Section titled “Minimum versions”](#minimum-versions)

`Database::connect` detects the engine and its version and refuses to start below these minimums (`Flavor::minimum_version` in `crates/verdin-db/src/lib.rs`):

| Engine     | Minimum   | Reason                                                                           |
| ---------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| PostgreSQL | 14        | Oldest version still supported upstream                                          |
| MySQL      | 8.4 LTS   | 8.0 reached end of life in April 2026                                            |
| MariaDB    | 10.11 LTS | Oldest current long-term release; `utf8mb4_uca1400_ai_ci` collation, usable JSON |
| SQLite     | 3.35      | `ALTER TABLE … DROP COLUMN`; the library is compiled into the binary             |

CI runs every test against PostgreSQL 14 and 17, MySQL 8.4, MariaDB 10.11 and 11.4, and SQLite. See [testing](/verdin/internals/testing/).

## Connecting

[Section titled “Connecting”](#connecting)

`verdin-db` wraps one `sqlx` pool per backend:

```rust
pub enum Pool { Postgres(PgPool), MySql(MySqlPool), Sqlite(SqlitePool) }


pub enum Flavor { Postgres, MySql, MariaDb, Sqlite }


pub struct Database { pool: Pool, flavor: Flavor, version: Version }
```

* URL schemes: `postgres://` or `postgresql://`, `mysql://`, `mariadb://` (an alias of `mysql://`) and `sqlite:`. MySQL and MariaDB share the `sqlx` MySQL driver; the flavor comes from `SELECT VERSION()`, which contains `MariaDB` on MariaDB.
* MySQL and MariaDB connections use `utf8mb4` and set the session time zone to `+00:00`, so every timestamp is stored in UTC.
* SQLite connections turn on foreign keys, use WAL journaling and a 5-second busy timeout, and create the database file (and its folder) if missing. In-memory databases get a single connection, because each connection to `:memory:` would open a different database.
* `ConnectOptions` sets the pool size (`[database].pool_max`, 10 by default) and the time to wait for a free connection (10 seconds).

`Flavor` carries the few facts the rest of the code branches on: `transactional_ddl()` (PostgreSQL and SQLite), `is_mysql_family()`, `quote(identifier)` (backticks on MySQL and MariaDB, double quotes elsewhere) and `minimum_version()`.

There is no dialect trait. Code that builds SQL checks the `Flavor` where the engines differ.

## Executing statements

[Section titled “Executing statements”](#executing-statements)

Three executors share the same methods (`execute`, `fetch_all`, `has_rows`, `insert_returning_id`):

| Executor                | Use                                                                          |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `db.queries()`          | One statement on any pooled connection                                       |
| `db.acquire()` → `Conn` | Several statements on one connection, such as a migration run holding a lock |
| `db.begin()` → `Tx`     | A transaction; dropped without `commit()`, it rolls back                     |

Statements are written with `?` placeholders, rewritten to `$1, $2…` for PostgreSQL. Values are `SqlValue`s, always bound as parameters. The SQL text itself may only contain identifiers that come from the validated schema, which is why it is passed to `sqlx` as `AssertSqlSafe`.

**Schema-driven decoding.** A read passes the `ColumnKind` of each selected column, and values are decoded by that kind, not by the type the driver reports. This is what makes MariaDB’s `JSON` (really `LONGTEXT`), MySQL’s `TINYINT(1)` booleans and SQLite’s text dates and decimals come back the same way on every engine. See `crates/verdin-db/src/value.rs`.

**Inserted ids.** `insert_returning_id` appends `RETURNING id` on PostgreSQL, and reads the id the driver reports after the insert on MySQL, MariaDB (`LAST_INSERT_ID`) and SQLite (`last_insert_rowid`).

**Unique violations.** `DbError::unique_violation()` extracts the index name (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB) or the column list (SQLite) from the driver error, so the Document Service can report a `ValidationError` on the right attribute.

## SQL builders

[Section titled “SQL builders”](#sql-builders)

Verdin builds SQL with its own small builders instead of an ORM or `sea-query`, because tables only exist at runtime (they come from the schema) and because the per-dialect details dominate: typed NULLs, collations, JSON functions and SQLite’s text formats.

| Crate                                   | Builds                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `verdin-migrate` (`sql.rs`, `Dialect`)  | DDL: column types, `CREATE TABLE`, `ALTER TABLE`, indexes, SQLite table rebuilds                   |
| `verdin-query` (`sql.rs`, `SqlBuilder`) | `WHERE` clauses for filters (including relation `EXISTS` subqueries and JSON paths) and `ORDER BY` |
| `verdin-content` (`service.rs`)         | Reads, inserts, updates, deletes, link table writes and batched populate queries                   |

A builder pushes SQL text and `ident()` names (quoted for the flavor) and collects parameters with `param()`, so building SQL and binding values happen in one place.

### Column types per dialect

[Section titled “Column types per dialect”](#column-types-per-dialect)

| Model type                | PostgreSQL                          | MySQL / MariaDB                  | SQLite                              |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| id                        | `bigint` identity                   | `bigint AUTO_INCREMENT`          | `integer PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` |
| integer, bigint, smallint | `integer`, `bigint`, `smallint`     | `int`, `bigint`, `smallint`      | `integer`                           |
| double                    | `double precision`                  | `double`                         | `real`                              |
| decimal                   | `numeric(p,s)`                      | `decimal(p,s)`                   | `text`                              |
| boolean                   | `boolean`                           | `tinyint(1)`                     | `integer`                           |
| char, varchar             | `char(n)`, `varchar(n)`             | `char(n)`, `varchar(n)`          | `text`                              |
| text                      | `text`                              | `longtext`                       | `text`                              |
| date, time, datetime      | `date`, `time(3)`, `timestamptz(3)` | `date`, `time(3)`, `datetime(3)` | `text`                              |
| json                      | `jsonb`                             | `json`                           | `text`                              |

SQLite stores dates and times as fixed-format text, so text order matches chronological order. It stores decimals as text too, so nothing is rounded when they are saved. Text order is not numeric order for decimals, so filters and sorts on a decimal cast the column to `REAL` on SQLite. Those comparisons are exact to about 15 significant digits, and the values returned are still exact. Which attribute maps to which model type is in [attribute types](/verdin/reference/attribute-types/).

MySQL and MariaDB tables are created with `ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4` and an accent- and case-insensitive collation: `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci` on MySQL, `utf8mb4_uca1400_ai_ci` on MariaDB.

## Dialect differences

[Section titled “Dialect differences”](#dialect-differences)

| Topic                                   | PostgreSQL             | MySQL 8.4                       | MariaDB                            | SQLite                 | How Verdin handles it                                                               |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Inserted id                             | `RETURNING`            | no `RETURNING`                  | driver id                          | driver id              | `insert_returning_id()`                                                             |
| Transactional DDL                       | yes                    | no (implicit commit)            | no                                 | yes                    | Step journal on MySQL and MariaDB (see [migrations](/verdin/internals/migrations/)) |
| JSON                                    | `jsonb`                | `json`                          | alias of `LONGTEXT`                | text                   | Schema-driven decoding                                                              |
| Booleans                                | `boolean`              | `tinyint(1)`                    | `tinyint(1)`                       | integer                | Schema-driven decoding                                                              |
| Datetime                                | `timestamptz`          | `datetime(3)`                   | `datetime(3)`                      | ISO text               | Always UTC; MySQL-family sessions use time zone `+00:00`                            |
| Charset and collation                   | UTF-8                  | `utf8mb4`, `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci` | `utf8mb4`, `utf8mb4_uca1400_ai_ci` | UTF-8, binary          | Set explicitly per table                                                            |
| Exact text match (`$eq`, `$in`…)        | `=`                    | `COLLATE utf8mb4_bin`           | same                               | `=`                    | Same results on every engine                                                        |
| `$contains`, `$startsWith`, `$endsWith` | `LIKE`                 | `LIKE … COLLATE utf8mb4_bin`    | same                               | `instr()` / `substr()` | SQLite’s `LIKE` ignores ASCII case, so it is not used for case-sensitive matches    |
| `$containsi` and other `…i` operators   | `ILIKE`                | `LIKE` (insensitive collation)  | same                               | `LIKE`                 | SQLite only folds ASCII case                                                        |
| JSON path filters                       | `#>>`                  | `JSON_VALUE`                    | same                               | `json_extract`         | Per-dialect operand                                                                 |
| JSON array filters                      | `jsonb_array_elements` | `JSON_TABLE`                    | same                               | `json_each`            | `EXISTS` over the items                                                             |
| `ALTER COLUMN`                          | full                   | `MODIFY COLUMN`                 | same                               | not supported          | SQLite: rebuild the table (create, copy, drop, rename)                              |
| Row locks                               | `FOR UPDATE`           | `FOR UPDATE`                    | `FOR UPDATE`                       | none                   | Omitted on SQLite, whose write transactions lock the database                       |
| Unique text index length                | —                      | 3,072 bytes                     | same                               | —                      | `varchar(255)` in `utf8mb4` is 1,020 bytes; `text` cannot be unique                 |
| Row size                                | —                      | 65,535 bytes                    | same                               | —                      | At most 60 `string`, `email`, `uid` or `enumeration` attributes per type            |

`LIKE` patterns escape `%`, `_` and the escape character itself (`!`) in user input. MySQL and MariaDB’s default collations ignore case and accents, which is why exact operators add a binary collation: `$eq` means the same thing on MySQL as on PostgreSQL. With JSON paths, `JSON_VALUE` returns a binary-collated string, so case-insensitive operators there compare `LOWER()` on both sides.

`ORDER BY` puts NULLs last in both directions and always ends with `id`, so pagination is stable on every engine.

# Decision log

> The design decisions behind Verdin, numbered in the order they were made, with the outcome and the reason for each.

This log records the design choices that shaped Verdin, in the order they were made, so you can see why the code is the way it is before proposing to change it. Entries are kept as they were written, milestone names included (M2–M4 are the milestones before the first releases); a later entry may refine an earlier one, as 28 does for 1. Add a new row when you make a decision that someone would otherwise have to reverse-engineer from the code.

| #  | Decision                         | Outcome                                                                                                                                                                             | Rationale                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -- | -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1  | Components: JSON vs tables       | **JSON column** ([storage](/verdin/internals/storage/#components-and-dynamic-zones-a-json-column))                                                                                  | Fewer joins, trivial publish/versioning, simpler migrations. Filtering on repeatable components is rare; can be added later with JSON functions                                                                                                                   |
| 2  | `decimal` JSON encoding          | **number** by default, `api.decimal_as_string` opt-in                                                                                                                               | Strapi compatibility maximises adoption; exact values available when needed                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 3  | Admin forms                      | **Signal Forms**                                                                                                                                                                    | Fits a signals-first, zoneless admin; dynamic form trees derived from the schema                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| 4  | Language                         | **English** for code, docs and commits                                                                                                                                              | Open source reach                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 5  | Strapi REST compatibility        | **Same parameters and response shape**; Verdin-only extensions under `actions/`                                                                                                     | Frontends migrate with minimal changes                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 6  | Admin JWT algorithm              | HS256                                                                                                                                                                               | Single secret, simple; EdDSA if external verifiers ever appear                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| 7  | Document IDs                     | ULID (26 chars)                                                                                                                                                                     | Sortable and portable; Strapi’s own ids are opaque 24-char strings, clients never parse them                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 8  | Snapshot content                 | Physical model, not schema                                                                                                                                                          | Later versions can derive new tables from an unchanged schema                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| 9  | Attribute nullability            | Always nullable; `required` checked on publish                                                                                                                                      | Drafts may be incomplete (Strapi v5 behaviour); adding required fields is safe                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| 10 | `unique` enforcement             | Unique index on `(column, locale, publication_state)`                                                                                                                               | Race-free; drafts and their published version share values                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| 11 | State column name                | `publication_state`                                                                                                                                                                 | `state` is a common attribute name                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| 12 | Reserved SQL words               | Always quote identifiers                                                                                                                                                            | No arbitrary blocklist of attribute names                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 13 | DML building                     | Own builder instead of `sea-query`                                                                                                                                                  | Per-dialect details dominate (typed NULLs, collations, SQLite formats); one less abstraction                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 14 | Writes without `?status=draft`   | Publish (Strapi v5 REST behaviour)                                                                                                                                                  | Drop-in compatibility for existing clients                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| 15 | Text comparison                  | Exact by default on every engine; `…i` operators for case-insensitive                                                                                                               | Same results on MySQL as on PostgreSQL                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 16 | Temporary access control (M2–M3) | `[api].open_access` switch, removed in M4                                                                                                                                           | Secure by default until permissions existed                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 17 | “Target belongs to one document” | Enforced by moving the target, per state                                                                                                                                            | A unique index would forbid a draft and its published version sharing a target                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| 18 | Inverse (`mappedBy`) sides       | Read-only                                                                                                                                                                           | Writing through them is ambiguous with draft & publish (which owner version?)                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| 19 | Link positions                   | Renumbered 1..n on each write                                                                                                                                                       | No float exhaustion; lists are small                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| 20 | Link table rows                  | Keep an `id` primary key                                                                                                                                                            | Uniform tables for the migration engine and SQLite rebuilds                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 21 | JWT library                      | Own HS256 (HMAC-SHA256, constant-time verify, `alg` pinned)                                                                                                                         | `jsonwebtoken` 11 needs a crypto backend that pulls RSA                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| 22 | Platform tables                  | Derived with the content model                                                                                                                                                      | One migration mechanism for everything                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 23 | Refresh token reuse              | Revoke the whole family, no grace window                                                                                                                                            | Simple and strict; the admin retries login                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| 24 | Drafts over the content API      | Separate `readDrafts` grant                                                                                                                                                         | Tokens that read published content do not leak drafts                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| 25 | Builder apply order              | Migrate, then write files, then hot-swap the app                                                                                                                                    | A failed migration leaves files and running app untouched                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 26 | Admin writes                     | Save drafts only; publishing is an explicit action                                                                                                                                  | Matches editors’ expectations; the content API keeps Strapi’s publish-by-default                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| 27 | Admin runtime config             | `<meta>` tag, not inline script                                                                                                                                                     | Keeps the CSP free of `unsafe-inline` scripts                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| 28 | Filters on component fields      | JSON path operators per dialect (`#>>`, `JSON_VALUE`, `json_extract`); `EXISTS` over array items for repeatable components and dynamic zones (0.8)                                  | Dynamic zones only by `__component`: their items have different fields                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 29 | Admin i18n                       | Transloco with flat JSON catalogs (`admin/public/i18n`) and ICU MessageFormat through FormatJS (a custom transpiler), behind a small `I18n` facade; not Angular’s compile-time i18n | Runtime language switch; standard files for Weblate/Crowdin; FormatJS interprets messages, so the strict CSP needs no `unsafe-eval` (`@messageformat/core` compiles with `new Function`); keys typed from `en.json`, completeness checked by `npm run i18n:check` |
| 30 | Week start                       | `Intl.Locale#getWeekInfo` of the browser’s regional tag (en-GB ≠ en-US), region table fallback, user override                                                                       | Follows each user’s region even when the UI language is shared                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| 31 | Dashboard layout storage         | Per-user JSON `preferences` column on `vd_admin_users` (≤ 64 KiB)                                                                                                                   | Follows the user across browsers; theme and language stay in `localStorage` because they apply before login                                                                                                                                                       |
| 32 | Refresh cookie `Secure` default  | On in `start`, off in `dev`, overridable                                                                                                                                            | `verdin dev` over plain HTTP works in every browser; production stays strict                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 33 | Release profile                  | Thin LTO, 1 codegen unit, stripped; unwinding kept                                                                                                                                  | A panicking handler must not take the server down                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 34 | “Unseen” documents               | Per-user `vd_document_views` rows, deleted for everyone but the editor when a document changes; filtered with `NOT EXISTS` in SQL                                                   | Pagination and counts stay exact; no timestamps to compare per row                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| 35 | Votes and polls                  | Admin-only collaboration tables (`vd_document_votes`, `vd_polls`, `vd_poll_votes`), any content type                                                                                | Suggestion boxes and team decisions without modelling vote fields in every schema                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 36 | Media storage                    | `object_store` for local and S3                                                                                                                                                     | One code path; streaming multipart uploads; RustFS in the dev stack and CI                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| 37 | Media links                      | Per-field link tables like relations                                                                                                                                                | Same draft/publish semantics as relations; cascades keep links consistent                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 38 | Built-in permission upgrades     | `vd_settings` version marker, additions applied once                                                                                                                                | Existing installs gain new permissions without undoing an admin’s later edits                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| 39 | Runtime features                 | Catalog in `verdin-api`, switches in `vd_settings` (`features`), the app rebuilt in place (ArcSwap) in every mode                                                                   | Strapi-like plugin switches without restarts; unavailable features are listed with their planned version                                                                                                                                                          |
| 40 | API reference UI                 | Scalar (`scalar_api_reference`, bundle embedded) at `{api}/docs`, only when the document is public; CSP allows its inline bootstrap by hash                                         | Self-hosted (no CDN, fonts, AI agent or telemetry); the document stays token-only by default                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 41 | GraphQL                          | `async-graphql` dynamic schema built with the app; arguments and selections are translated to the REST parameter tree and parsed by the same query parser                           | One set of rules for filters, pagination, populate, validation and permissions across REST and GraphQL; populate derived from the selection keeps batched loading                                                                                                 |
| 42 | Document events                  | Listeners on the Document Service, called after commit                                                                                                                              | Side effects (seen marks, future webhooks) apply to every API without per-handler hooks                                                                                                                                                                           |

# Document Service

> The single internal API that reads and writes content in Verdin, what it guarantees on every write, and the path a content API request takes to reach it.

The Document Service (`DocumentService` in `crates/verdin-content/src/service.rs`) is the only code that reads and writes content rows. The content API, the admin API, GraphQL, MCP, plugins, imports and the sitemap all go through it, so validation, draft and publish, relation rules and events behave the same whichever API made the call. Like Strapi v5’s Document Service, it works on documents (identified by `documentId`), not on rows.

## API

[Section titled “API”](#api)

The main methods (simplified; see the source for the exact types):

| Method                                               | Does                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `find_many(uid, &Query) -> Page`                     | A page of documents, with `meta` in page or offset form                                     |
| `find_one(uid, document_id, &Query) -> Option<Json>` | One document in the query’s status and locale                                               |
| `single_document_id(uid)`                            | The document of a single type, if it exists                                                 |
| `create(uid, &data, WriteOptions) -> String`         | Creates a document and returns its `documentId`                                             |
| `update(uid, document_id, &data, WriteOptions)`      | Partial update of the draft (or the only version); creates a new locale version when needed |
| `delete(uid, document_id)`                           | Deletes every version of the document in the current locale                                 |
| `publish(uid, document_id, actor)`                   | Copies the draft onto the published version                                                 |
| `unpublish(uid, document_id)`                        | Deletes the published version                                                               |
| `discard_draft(uid, document_id)`                    | Replaces the draft with the published version                                               |
| `uid_availability(…)`                                | Whether a `uid` value is free, with a free suggestion                                       |
| `document_locales`, `timeline`, `usage`…             | Helpers for the admin panel                                                                 |

`WriteOptions` has two fields: `publish` (publish after writing, on draft and publish types) and `actor` (the admin recorded in `created_by_id` / `updated_by_id`).

The service is a cheap-to-clone value configured with builder methods: `in_locale(locale)` for localized types, `with_listener`, `with_hook`, `dry_run()` (validate a write in full and roll it back, used by import dry runs) and `without_plugin_hooks()` (for writes plugins make themselves).

It does not know who is calling. Permissions are applied by the API layer before the call: it refuses actions the caller lacks, restricts which types a query may populate or filter through, and adds condition filters to the query (for example the admin **Author** role’s “own entries” condition becomes `created_by_id = <admin id>`). Filters are part of the SQL, so pagination and counts stay exact.

## What every write does

[Section titled “What every write does”](#what-every-write-does)

1. **Hooks.** `DocumentHook`s run first, in order: review workflow stages, then plugins. A hook may replace the data or refuse the write, which becomes a `400`. They use Strapi’s lifecycle names (`beforeCreate`, `beforeUpdate`, `beforeDelete`, `beforePublish`, `beforeUnpublish`, `beforeDiscardDraft`).
2. **Validation of the input** (`input.rs`): unknown keys, system fields (`id`, `documentId`, timestamps) and inverse (`mappedBy`) relation sides are errors; every value is checked against its attribute type and constraints (`min`, `max`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `regex`, enumeration values, relation cardinality, media `allowedTypes`); components and dynamic zones are validated recursively; `password` values are hashed with argon2.
3. **References.** Related documents and media files must exist, checked inside the transaction.
4. **Rows and links**, in one transaction: the row is inserted or updated, then its relation, polymorphic and media link tables are rewritten (positions renumbered 1..n). Linking a `oneToOne` or `oneToMany` target moves it away from other documents in the same state.
5. **Required fields and rules.** When a version becomes published, or on every write to types without draft and publish, `required` attributes (including those inside components and dynamic zones) and cross-field validation rules are checked. A failure rolls the whole write back.
6. **Uniqueness** is enforced by the scoped unique indexes. A violation is mapped back to its attribute and reported as a `ValidationError`, race-free.
7. **Commit, then events.** After the transaction commits, the service calls every `DocumentListener` with a `DocumentEvent` (`entry.create`, `entry.update`, `entry.publish`, `entry.unpublish`, `entry.discard-draft`, `entry.delete`), carrying the uid, `documentId`, locale and actor.

Validation errors use Strapi’s format: a list of `{ path, message, name: "ValidationError" }`, where `path` points into the data (`["seo", "metaTitle"]`, `["blocks", 2, "text"]`). The admin panel maps them back onto its fields.

Listeners keep derived state in step with content without per-handler code: webhooks, content history, the response cache, plugins’ after-write hooks, the audit log, realtime events, comments and tasks, “seen” marks, CDN purges and the search index. A listener that fails logs its own error; the write has already succeeded. Because listeners run after the commit, a dry run never reaches them.

## Reads

[Section titled “Reads”](#reads)

A read selects the rows of the requested status and locale, applies filters and sort in SQL, and then populates what was asked for:

* **Relations** are loaded with batched queries, one per relation and level (`WHERE … IN (…)`, in chunks of 500 ids), never with cascading joins. That avoids both cartesian explosions and N+1 queries. At most 1,000 related entries are populated per entry and relation; counts stay exact.
* Targets are read in the same version as the source: published documents see published targets, drafts see drafts.
* **Components and dynamic zones** come from their JSON column; relations and media inside them are resolved with the same batched queries.
* **`_q` search** uses the Tantivy index when `[search]` is on, and a case-insensitive `$containsi` over the text fields otherwise.

How the output looks (flat documents, value formats, `populate` syntax, limits) is documented in the [REST API](/verdin/api/rest/).

## Content API request lifecycle

[Section titled “Content API request lifecycle”](#content-api-request-lifecycle)

```
sequenceDiagram
participant C as Client
participant L as Shared layers
participant H as handlers.rs
participant Q as verdin-query
participant D as Document Service
participant DB as Database
C->>L: GET /api/articles?filters…
L->>H: client IP, request id, CORS, limits, cache
H->>H: route by pluralName, authorize token or public role
H->>Q: parse and validate against the schema
Q-->>H: typed Query
H->>D: find_many(uid, query)
D->>DB: SELECT … WHERE … ORDER BY … LIMIT
D->>DB: one batched query per populated relation
D-->>H: documents and page meta
H-->>C: { data, meta }
```

A GET /api/articles request, from the socket to the database

1. **Shared layers** (outermost first): the client address is resolved (using `X-Forwarded-For` only from `[server].trusted_proxies`), metrics count the request when enabled, a request id is set and propagated as `x-request-id`, tracing opens a span, and CORS applies to the content API and GraphQL when `[api].cors_origins` is set.
2. **Content API layers**: rate limits per client, `ETag`s and the optional cache of anonymous reads, the body size limit (`[server].body_limit`) and request timeout, CDN cache tags on responses.
3. **Routing.** The path segment is looked up among the content types’ `pluralName`s (collection types) and `singularName`s (single types). Unknown names are `404`.
4. **Authorization** (`verdin-auth`). No `Authorization` header means the public role; `Bearer vd_…` is an API token. An invalid or expired token is `401`, never the public role. The route’s action (`find`, `findOne`, `create`, `update`, `delete`, `publish`) must be granted for the type, or the answer is `403`.
5. **Query parsing** (`verdin-query`). The raw query string is parsed into a bracket tree (at most 16 KB, 12 levels, 1,000 pairs), then into a typed `Query` validated against the type’s fields: unknown and `private` fields are `400`, and populate, relation filters and relation sorts are limited to types the caller may read. Reading `?status=draft` also needs `readDrafts`.
6. **Document Service.** The handler calls `find_many`, `find_one`, `create`, `update`, `delete` or an action. Writes without `?status=draft` publish on draft and publish types (Strapi v5 behaviour), and read back the written version for the response.
7. **Response.** `{ "data": …, "meta": … }`. Errors use the same envelope with `data: null` and an `error` object.

Admin API routes follow the same path with an admin session instead of an API token, admin RBAC instead of content API grants, and draft-first defaults: they read drafts and write drafts only, and publishing is an explicit action. GraphQL translates its arguments into the same parameter tree before step 5, so it shares the parser, the limits and the permission rules.

# Migration engine

> How Verdin turns schema changes into DDL, classifies each step by risk, and applies plans safely on engines with and without transactional DDL.

This page explains how `verdin-migrate` brings the database in line with the schema: how it computes the difference, how it rates each step, and how it applies a plan so that a failure never leaves you guessing. For the day-to-day workflow (`verdin migrate plan`, `--allow`, renames), read [schema migrations](/verdin/concepts/schema-migrations/) first; command flags are in the [CLI reference](/verdin/reference/cli/).

## Flow

[Section titled “Flow”](#flow)

```
flowchart LR
Files["schema/*.json"] -->|parse, validate| Schema
Schema -->|derive| Desired["DbModel<br/>desired"]
Snapshot[("vd_schema_snapshots")] --> Current["DbModel<br/>current"]
Current --> Diff{"diff"}
Desired --> Diff
Diff -->|changes| Plan["plan for the Flavor<br/>steps, risk, SQL, pre-checks"]
Plan -->|apply| Db[("database")]
```

From schema files to applied DDL

1. `verdin-schema` parses and validates the files into a `Schema`.
2. `derive_model` (`derive.rs`) turns it into a `DbModel`: every table, column, index and foreign key the schema needs, including link tables and the [platform tables](/verdin/internals/storage/#platform-tables).
3. The last applied model is read from `vd_schema_snapshots`.
4. `diff` (`diff.rs`) compares the two models and returns a list of `Change`s, plus rename hints.
5. `build_plan` (`plan.rs`) renders each change into SQL for the connected flavor, rates it, and attaches a pre-check where one is needed.
6. `apply` (`apply.rs`) runs the plan, then stores the desired model as the new snapshot.

**The snapshot stores the physical model, not the schema.** When a later Verdin version derives more tables from the same schema (link tables for a new feature, a new platform table), the diff creates them without any schema change.

**The diff runs against the snapshot, not against the live database.** That keeps it deterministic and avoids the differences in how each engine reports its own structure. Verdin does not introspect the database, so manual changes to the tables (drift) are not detected.

Changes that render to the same DDL on a dialect produce no step. For example, `string` → `text` is a type change on PostgreSQL and MySQL, but both are `text` on SQLite, so SQLite gets no step.

## Change categories

[Section titled “Change categories”](#change-categories)

Every step has a risk level (`Risk` in `diff.rs`). `apply` only runs steps up to the level you allow, and refuses the whole plan before running anything if a step is above it.

| Risk            | Changes                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Safe**        | Create a table; add a nullable or defaulted column; relax a column (make it nullable, same type and default); create a non-unique index, or a unique index on a new table; drop an index; rename a table or column |
| **Risky**       | Add a `NOT NULL` column without a default; change a column’s type, nullability or default otherwise; add a unique index to an existing table; rebuild a SQLite table without dropping columns                      |
| **Destructive** | Drop a column; drop a table; rebuild a SQLite table that drops columns                                                                                                                                             |

Because every attribute column is nullable (see [storage](/verdin/internals/storage/#system-columns)), adding attributes, including required ones, is always safe. `enumeration` values are checked by the application, not by the column, so adding or removing a value changes no DDL at all.

**Pre-checks** run before the first statement of a plan, so a risky step that cannot succeed stops the run while the database is untouched:

| Step                                | Pre-check                                           |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Unique index on an existing table   | No duplicate non-NULL values in the indexed columns |
| `NOT NULL` column without a default | The table has no rows                               |
| Column becomes `NOT NULL`           | The column has no NULLs                             |

**Renames.** A dropped column plus an added column of the same column type in the same table is *proposed* as a rename: `verdin migrate plan` prints a hint such as `--rename-column articles.title=headline`, and the content-type builder offers to accept it. It is never inferred silently; without the flag, the plan drops the old column and adds a new one. A dropped table plus a created table with the same columns gets a `--rename-table old=new` hint the same way. Renames are safe steps, and a renamed table takes its link tables with it.

**SQLite rebuilds.** SQLite cannot alter a column, so when a table has any column alteration the planner replaces all of that table’s column and index changes with one rebuild: create the new shape under a temporary name, copy the surviving columns, drop the old table, rename the new one, recreate the indexes.

## Modes

[Section titled “Modes”](#modes)

| Command                                  | What happens                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `verdin start`                           | Pending steps stop the boot with a message that points to `verdin migrate plan`. The schema files are read-only.                                                                                      |
| `verdin start --migrate`                 | Pending **safe** steps apply before the server starts; anything riskier stops the boot.                                                                                                               |
| `verdin dev`                             | Safe steps apply at boot. A file watcher on `schema/` reloads on every change: safe migrations apply and the app is swapped in place; riskier changes are logged and the running app stays as it was. |
| Content-type builder (`verdin dev` only) | `POST /schema/plan` shows the steps, their risk, their SQL and rename hints. `POST /schema/apply` runs them at the risk level the user confirmed.                                                     |
| `verdin migrate plan`                    | Prints each step with its risk and its exact SQL for the connected dialect, the `--allow` level the plan needs, and rename hints.                                                                     |
| `verdin migrate apply`                   | Runs the plan. `--allow risky` or `--allow destructive` is required when the plan contains such steps.                                                                                                |

When the builder applies a change, it migrates first, then writes `schema/*.json`, then swaps the app. If the migration fails, the files and the running app stay as they were. Because the builder’s output is files, the flow ends in a git commit.

## Execution that survives non-transactional DDL

[Section titled “Execution that survives non-transactional DDL”](#execution-that-survives-non-transactional-ddl)

PostgreSQL and SQLite run DDL inside transactions. MySQL and MariaDB commit implicitly on every DDL statement, so a failure halfway through a plan would leave the database between two states. `apply` handles both.

**On every engine:**

1. Take the migration lock on one dedicated connection: `pg_advisory_lock` on PostgreSQL; `GET_LOCK('verdin_migrate:<database>')` on MySQL and MariaDB, waiting up to 60 seconds; on SQLite, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` serializes writers. On SQLite the engine also turns `foreign_keys` off for the run, so table rebuilds do not cascade into link tables.
2. Recompute the plan from the snapshot, and check the allowed risk.
3. Run every pre-check before the first DDL statement.

**On PostgreSQL and SQLite**, the whole plan, the new snapshot and a `completed` journal row run in a single transaction. A failure rolls everything back.

**On MySQL and MariaDB**, every step is a single statement, and progress is recorded step by step:

1. Record the plan in `vd_migrations_journal` (the plan’s hash and its steps) with status `running`.
2. Execute each step and record the number of completed steps after each one.
3. If a step fails, the journal keeps the error and stays `running`. `verdin migrate plan` then reports the interrupted run, how many steps were applied and the last error.
4. The next `apply` recomputes the plan. If its hash matches the journal, it **resumes** from the failed step: single DDL statements are atomic on these engines, so the failed step runs again. Pre-checks are skipped on resume, because earlier steps already changed the database.
5. If the schema changed in the meantime, the hashes differ and `apply` refuses, asking you to restore the schema the plan was made from.
6. When the last step succeeds, the new snapshot and the journal’s `completed` status are written together in one transaction.

The plan hash covers the flavor and every statement, so a resumed run executes exactly the SQL that was planned.

# Architecture overview

> How Verdin is built, from its design principles to the crates a request passes through, for contributors who want to read or change the code.

This section is for people who work on Verdin itself. It explains how the server and the admin panel are put together, why they are built that way, and where to start reading the code. To use Verdin, start with the [quickstart](/verdin/start/quickstart/) instead.

Verdin is a headless CMS written in Rust that follows Strapi v5: you model content visually or in JSON files, and you get a REST and GraphQL API plus an admin panel. It ships as one binary that holds the server, the CLI and the Angular admin panel, and it runs on PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite.

## Goals

[Section titled “Goals”](#goals)

* **One binary.** `verdin` contains the server, the CLI and the embedded admin panel. Production needs no Node.js and no `node_modules`.
* **Fast startup, small memory footprint.**
* **Four databases, one test suite.** PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite are all first-class and all covered by the same tests.
* **Schema as code.** Content types are JSON files that you version in git.
* **Strapi v5 compatible REST API** wherever reasonable, so existing frontends move over with few changes.
* **Everything free.** There is no enterprise edition: SSO, audit logs, review workflows, releases and every other feature ship for everyone.

What has shipped release by release, and what comes next, is in the [roadmap](/verdin/project/roadmap/).

### Non-goals
