| Content history          | Supported | `[history].max_versions` versions per document.                                                                                                                              |
| Preview and live preview | Supported | Preview URLs with short-lived tokens, side-by-side preview and [visual editing](/verdin/guides/frontend/visual-editing/).                                                    |
| Custom admin roles       | Supported | No limit on their number.                                                                                                                                                    |

# Migrating from Strapi

> Move a Strapi v4 or v5 project to Verdin with verdin import strapi — export, import, what comes across, the id map, checks afterwards and the changes your frontend needs.

`verdin import strapi` brings a Strapi v4 or v5 project into Verdin: its content types and components become schema files, and its entries, locales, media library, relations, end users and public permissions are imported. This page walks through a migration and lists what your frontend has to change. For a feature-by-feature comparison, see [Strapi compatibility](/verdin/migrate/compatibility/).

```
flowchart LR
S[Strapi project] -->|strapi export| E[export .tar.gz]
E -->|verdin import strapi| F[schema files]
F --> M[migrate database]
M --> D[entries, media, users]
D --> R[strapi-id-map.json]
```

The importer reads Strapi's export file; it never connects to the Strapi database.

## Before you start

[Section titled “Before you start”](#before-you-start)

* A Strapi v4 or v5 project where you can run `strapi export`.
* A new Verdin project (`verdin new my-site`), or one without schema files of the same names. See the [quickstart](/verdin/start/quickstart/).
* The database and media storage the Verdin project will use in production, if you can: files are copied into the configured upload provider during the import.

## 1. Export from Strapi

[Section titled “1. Export from Strapi”](#1-export-from-strapi)

In the Strapi project:

```sh
npx strapi export --no-encrypt -f my-export      # writes my-export.tar.gz
```

Verdin cannot read encrypted exports (`.tar.gz.enc`); export again with `--no-encrypt`. Uncompressed exports (`--no-compress`, a `.tar`) and an unpacked export directory work too.

## 2. Import into Verdin

[Section titled “2. Import into Verdin”](#2-import-into-verdin)

1. Create the project and import the export:

   ```sh
   verdin new my-site && cd my-site
   verdin import strapi ../my-export.tar.gz
   ```

2. Read the summary. The importer prints how many documents, versions, files, folders, locales and links it imported, then one line per warning.

3. Start the development server and open the admin panel:

   ```sh
   verdin dev
   ```

The command runs these steps in order:

1. Writes one schema file per `api::` content type and per component to `schema/`. If the converted schema does not validate, nothing is written.
2. Migrates the database (safe steps).
3. Imports locales, media folders and files, entries (every draft, published version and locale), relations, and the media attached to entries and components.
4. Imports end users, their roles and the public and authenticated permissions.
5. Writes `strapi-id-map.json` in the project directory.

| Option          | Effect                                                                                    |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--schema-only` | Stop after writing the schema files. Useful to review or adjust the schema first.         |
| `--force`       | Overwrite existing schema files, and import into content types that already have entries. |

Without `--force`, the import stops if a schema file it would write already exists, or if a content type already has entries.

## What comes across

[Section titled “What comes across”](#what-comes-across)

| Strapi                                                                       | Verdin                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `api::…` content types and components                                        | Schema files, keeping `collectionName`, draft and publish, i18n options and field options (`required`, `private`, `unique`, lengths, `regex`, defaults…) |
| Relations between `api::` types                                              | The same relations                                                                                                                                       |
| Relations inside components                                                  | `oneWay` / `manyWay` references                                                                                                                          |
| Polymorphic relations (`morphToOne`, `morphToMany`, `morphOne`, `morphMany`) | The same, with their links to imported content types                                                                                                     |
| Media fields (also in components)                                            | Media fields                                                                                                                                             |
| v5 rows (draft and published)                                                | Draft and published versions                                                                                                                             |
| v4 rows                                                                      | A draft, plus a published version when `publishedAt` is set; `localizations` become locales of one document                                              |
| `plugin::i18n.locale`                                                        | Locales (Strapi’s default stays the default)                                                                                                             |
| `plugin::upload.file` and `folder`                                           | Media library files (with their formats) and folders                                                                                                     |
| `password` fields                                                            | `password` fields, keeping Strapi’s bcrypt hashes                                                                                                        |
| Custom fields (`customField`)                                                | The attribute with its `customField` kept; see below                                                                                                     |
| Conditional fields (`conditions`, Strapi 5.17)                               | Kept in the schema and applied by the editor                                                                                                             |
| `plugin::users-permissions.user`                                             | End users, with their bcrypt passwords (re-hashed with Argon2id at the next sign-in), `confirmed` and `blocked`                                          |
| Users & Permissions roles                                                    | The Public role’s grants become Verdin’s public permissions; Authenticated and custom roles become end-user roles                                        |
| Role permissions on content types and uploads                                | `find`, `findOne`, `create`, `update` and `delete` grants; upload `find`, `findOne`, `upload` and `destroy`                                              |

## What does not come across

[Section titled “What does not come across”](#what-does-not-come-across)

Reported as warnings:

* Relations to admin users, end users or other plugins’ types (only `api::` targets are imported). The `createdBy` / `updatedBy` fields are left out.
* `unique` on `text`, `richtext`, `blocks` and `json` attributes (Verdin supports it on short text types).
* Attribute types Verdin does not know, and relation types it cannot store inside a component.
* Relation halves whose `inversedBy` / `mappedBy` do not match the other side.
* Locale codes that are not valid.

Not imported at all: admin users and admin roles, API tokens, transfer tokens, webhooks, releases, review workflow stages, content history and audit logs, and the settings of Strapi plugins. Your Strapi code — controllers, services, routes, policies, middlewares, lifecycle hooks, cron tasks and admin customizations — is not converted: rebuild it as described in [Rebuild custom code](#rebuild-custom-code).

Note

Custom fields keep their `customField` name, such as `plugin::color-picker.color`. The editor shows them with a [plugin](/verdin/extending/plugins/) that provides that field, and falls back to the input for the stored type when none does.

## The id map

[Section titled “The id map”](#the-id-map)

Verdin generates new document ids: Strapi’s `documentId`s have 24 characters and Verdin’s have 26, so every document gets a new one. Numeric `id`s change too. `strapi-id-map.json` records the mapping:

strapi-id-map.json

```json
{
  "documents": {
    "api::article": {
      "hq7xw1c6m2vkn0f3t8ybz5sd": "01k6b3xg0r9m2m7c1d4e5f6g7h"
    }
  },
  "files": {
    "12": 3
  }
}
```

* `documents` is keyed by the Verdin content type uid (`api::article`, Strapi’s `api::article.article`), then by the Strapi `documentId` (v5) or by a row id (v4: one id stands for all the locales of a document).
* `files` maps Strapi file ids to Verdin file ids.

Use it to rewrite ids stored outside the CMS: links in your frontend’s code, ids in another database, analytics, bookmarks.

## Check the result

[Section titled “Check the result”](#check-the-result)

1. `verdin schema check` passes, and `verdin migrate plan` says the database is up to date.
2. In the admin panel, open each collection and compare the number of entries, drafts and locales with Strapi.
3. Open a few entries with relations, components, dynamic zones and media, and check that the links point to the right documents and files.
4. Open the **Media library** and check that folders and images (with their formats) are there.
5. In **Settings → Public access** and **Settings → End users**, review the imported permissions and roles.
6. Call your API as your frontend does and compare the responses with Strapi’s.

Then commit `schema/`, create your admins, API tokens and webhooks, and deploy (see the [production checklist](/verdin/deploy/production-checklist/)).

## Frontend changes

[Section titled “Frontend changes”](#frontend-changes)

The content API follows Strapi v5’s REST and GraphQL shapes, so most requests work as they are. Change these:

* **Base URL.** Point the frontend at the Verdin server. The content API is under `/api` (`[api].prefix`), GraphQL at `/graphql` once you turn it on in **Settings → Features**.
* **API tokens.** Tokens are not imported: create new ones in **Settings → API tokens** and replace them in your frontend’s environment.
* **Document ids.** Every `documentId` and numeric `id` is new. Replace ids hard-coded in the frontend with the ones in `strapi-id-map.json`, or better, look entries up by a slug or another `uid` field.
* **Media URLs.** File URLs point at the new provider: `/uploads/…` on the Verdin server for the local provider, or `[upload.provider].public_url` for S3. Update image domains allowed by your framework (for example `images.remotePatterns` in Next.js).
* **Signed-in end users** must sign in again: their passwords work, but JWTs issued by Strapi do not.
* **CORS.** If a browser calls the API from another origin, list it in `[api].cors_origins`.
* **Webhooks.** Recreate them in **Settings → Webhooks**. Strapi’s `entry.draft-discard` event is called `entry.discard-draft`, and deliveries are signed (see [Webhooks](/verdin/guides/integrations/webhooks/)).
* **Strapi v4 frontends** need the v5 changes too: flat responses without `attributes`, `documentId` instead of `id` in URLs, and `status=draft` instead of `publicationState=preview`.

For typed access, generate TypeScript types with `verdin types` and use the [typed client](/verdin/guides/frontend/typed-client/).

## Rebuild custom code

[Section titled “Rebuild custom code”](#rebuild-custom-code)

Code in `src/` moves to a [WebAssembly plugin](/verdin/extending/plugins/). [Porting custom code](/verdin/migrate/porting-custom-code/) walks through a real project’s lifecycles, routes, cron task and `bootstrap`, with a worked example plugin.

| Strapi                                                                | Verdin                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Lifecycle hooks, document service middlewares                         | Plugin hooks (`beforeCreate`, `afterUpdate`…)                                                             |
| Custom routes and controllers                                         | Plugin routes under `/api/plugins/<name>/`                                                                |
| `bootstrap()` in `src/index.js` (seeding, setting public permissions) | The plugin’s startup function (`[startup]`), with the `public_permissions` capability for the public role |
| Cron tasks                                                            | Plugin jobs (`[[jobs]]`)                                                                                  |
| A custom endpoint that stores form submissions                        | Built-in [Forms](/verdin/guides/frontend/forms/)                                                          |
| Custom fields                                                         | Plugin custom fields                                                                                      |
| Admin widgets                                                         | Plugin widgets, or the built-in dashboard widgets                                                         |
| Admin logo, colors and texts                                          | `[admin.branding]` in `verdin.toml`                                                                       |
| `config/*.js`                                                         | `verdin.toml` and environment variables ([configuration reference](/verdin/reference/configuration/))     |

# Porting custom code

> Move a Strapi project's custom code to a Verdin plugin — controllers and routes, lifecycles, services, bootstrap, cron tasks, admin widgets, forms, policies and middlewares — with a worked example and the limits to plan around.

`verdin import strapi` brings over a Strapi project’s schema and content, but not the JavaScript in `src/`: Verdin runs no JavaScript on the server. That code becomes a [WebAssembly plugin](/verdin/extending/plugins/): hooks for lifecycles, routes for custom controllers, a startup function for `bootstrap`, jobs for cron tasks. This page maps each kind of Strapi code to its Verdin counterpart, walks through a real project’s code ported to a plugin, and lists the limits to plan around.

The worked example is [`examples/strapi-port`](https://github.com/Verdin-CMS/verdin/tree/main/examples/strapi-port): the `tienda` plugin, written in Rust, with the schema it needs and a README that builds and installs it. Read the [plugin tutorial](/verdin/extending/plugin-tutorial/) first if you have never written a plugin; the [plugin reference](/verdin/extending/plugin-reference/) has every payload and host function.

## Where each piece goes

[Section titled “Where each piece goes”](#where-each-piece-goes)

| Strapi                                                            | Verdin                                                                           | Notes                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Custom routes and controllers (`src/api/*/routes`, `controllers`) | Plugin routes: `[routes]`, one function for `/api/plugins/<name>/…`              | The URL changes. The function dispatches on method and path itself.                           |
| Lifecycles (`lifecycles.js`), Document Service middlewares        | `[[hooks]]` on `beforeCreate`, `afterUpdate`…                                    | Same event names. Before hooks can replace the data or refuse the write.                      |
| Services (`src/api/*/services`)                                   | Functions in the plugin’s module, and `verdin_content` for `strapi.documents(…)` | No shared services between plugins.                                                           |
| `bootstrap()` in `src/index.js`                                   | `[startup]` function                                                             | Runs at start, when the plugin is switched on and when its settings change.                   |
| `register()`                                                      | Nothing to port                                                                  | The manifest declares what `register` set up.                                                 |
| Cron tasks (`config/cron-tasks.js`)                               | `[[jobs]]`                                                                       | Cron syntax in UTC, seconds optional.                                                         |
| Plugin configuration (`config/plugins.js`)                        | `[[settings]]` and `verdin_config`                                               | Edited in **Settings → Plugins**.                                                             |
| `strapi.log`                                                      | `verdin_log`                                                                     | Server log and **Settings → Plugins → Logs**.                                                 |
| Admin widgets (`app.widgets.register`)                            | `[[admin.widgets]]`: Web Components                                              | Or the built-in dashboard widgets.                                                            |
| Custom fields                                                     | `[[admin.fields]]`                                                               | The `customField` name in the schema is kept.                                                 |
| Injection zones, custom admin pages, React extensions             | Not supported                                                                    | Branding is in `[admin.branding]`.                                                            |
| A custom endpoint that stores form submissions                    | Built-in [Forms](/verdin/guides/frontend/forms/)                                 | Validation, spam trap, rate limit, emails and CSV export included.                            |
| Policies and middlewares                                          | Built-in permissions, rate limits and CORS; checks in your plugin routes         | No hook into the request pipeline. See [Policies and middlewares](#policies-and-middlewares). |
| Emails from code (`strapi.plugin('email')`)                       | An email provider’s HTTP API, through the `http` capability                      | No email host function.                                                                       |

## The example project

[Section titled “The example project”](#the-example-project)

The Strapi project behind the example is a small shop with polls:

* **`producto`**: products, with `a_la_venta` (on sale) and `reservable` flags.
* **`reserva`**: reservations sent by visitors. A `beforeCreate` lifecycle forces `estado` to `pendiente`, checks that the related product is on sale and reservable, and clamps `unidades` to 1–10.
* **`encuesta`** and **`voto`**: polls with a list of options, and their votes. Two custom routes, `POST /api/polls/:slug/vote` and `GET /api/polls/:slug/results`, allow one vote per visitor and poll, only in open polls and only for a valid option. A cron task closes polls whose `cierra_el` date has passed.
* **`bootstrap`** sets the public role’s permissions, so a fresh install is not left open.
* An **admin widget** shows the open polls.

In Verdin all of it is one plugin, `tienda`:

* examples/strapi-port/

  * verdin.toml

  * schema/

    * content-types/ producto, reserva, encuesta, voto

      * …

  * plugin/

    * Cargo.toml
    * plugin.toml the manifest
    * src/lib.rs hooks, routes, the job and the startup function
    * admin/index.js the dashboard widget

plugin/plugin.toml (abridged)

```toml
name = "tienda"
version = "0.1.0"


[capabilities]
read = ["api::producto"]
write = ["api::voto", "api::encuesta"]
public_permissions = true


[[hooks]]
on = "beforeCreate"
uid = "api::reserva"
function = "before_create_reserva"


[routes]
function = "handle"


[[jobs]]
schedule = "*/15 * * * *"
function = "close_polls"


[startup]
function = "startup"
```

Content type uids are shorter than Strapi’s: `api::producto`, not `api::producto.producto`.

## Lifecycles to hooks

[Section titled “Lifecycles to hooks”](#lifecycles-to-hooks)

The Strapi lifecycle, simplified:

src/api/reserva/content-types/reserva/lifecycles.js

```js
const { errors } = require('@strapi/utils');


module.exports = {
  async beforeCreate(event) {
    const { data } = event.params;
    data.estado = 'pendiente';
    const documentId = data.producto?.connect?.[0]?.documentId ?? data.producto;
    const producto = await strapi.documents('api::producto.producto').findOne({ documentId });
    if (!producto?.a_la_venta || !producto.reservable) {
      throw new errors.ApplicationError('This product cannot be reserved');
    }
    data.unidades = Math.min(Math.max(parseInt(data.unidades, 10) || 1, 1), 10);
  },
};
```

The Verdin hook receives `{ event, uid, documentId, locale, data }` and answers `{ "data": … }` to replace what is written, `{ "error": "…" }` to refuse the write (the client gets a 400 with the message, as with Strapi’s `ApplicationError`), or `{}` to let it through:

plugin/src/lib.rs (abridged)

```rust
#[plugin_fn]
pub fn before_create_reserva(Json(input): Json<Value>) -> FnResult<Json<Value>> {
    let mut data = input["data"].clone();
    data["estado"] = json!("pendiente");


    let Some(producto_id) = relation_id(&data["producto"]) else {
        return Ok(Json(json!({ "error": "Choose a product to reserve" })));
    };
    let found = content(json!({ "op": "findOne", "uid": "api::producto", "documentId": producto_id }))?;
    let producto = &found["document"];
    if producto.is_null() {
        return Ok(Json(json!({ "error": "The product does not exist or is not published" })));
    }
    if producto["a_la_venta"] != true {
        return Ok(Json(json!({ "error": "The product is not on sale" })));
    }
    if producto["reservable"] != true {
        return Ok(Json(json!({ "error": "The product cannot be reserved" })));
    }


    let max = settings()["maxUnidades"].as_i64().unwrap_or(10).max(1);
    let unidades = as_number(&data["unidades"]).map_or(1, |n| n.round() as i64);
    data["unidades"] = json!(unidades.clamp(1, max));
    Ok(Json(json!({ "data": data })))
}
```

Things to know when porting lifecycles:

* **`data` is the request’s data as sent.** A relation can arrive as a documentId, as `{ "documentId": … }`, as a list, or as `{ connect }` / `{ set }` (the admin panel and clients differ). The example’s `relation_id` accepts all of them. On `beforeUpdate`, `data` holds only the fields sent.
* **The data you return is validated** like the original, after the hook: a hook cannot write something the schema refuses. Schema bounds (`min`, `max`) refuse a value; a hook can clamp it instead, as here.
* **Hooks do not know who is writing.** There is no user or token in the input. Checks that depend on the caller belong in the permissions, or in a plugin route.
* **After hooks get no data**: `{ event, uid, documentId, locale }`, sent once the write is committed. Read the entry with `verdin_content` if you need it.
* **A failing hook does not block the write.** If the module traps or times out, the error is logged and the write goes on; only an `{ error }` answer refuses it.
* **Writes made by plugins skip before hooks.** A rule that must hold for every write must also be applied by any plugin code that writes that type.

## Controllers and custom routes to plugin routes

[Section titled “Controllers and custom routes to plugin routes”](#controllers-and-custom-routes-to-plugin-routes)

Strapi served the poll routes at `/api/polls/:slug/vote`. A Verdin plugin serves everything under `/api/plugins/<name>/`, so the frontend calls `/api/plugins/tienda/polls/:slug/vote` (or a reverse proxy rewrites the old path). One exported function receives every request and dispatches on method and path:

plugin/src/lib.rs (abridged)

```rust
#[plugin_fn]
pub fn handle(Json(request): Json<Value>) -> FnResult<Json<Value>> {
    let method = request["method"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
    let path = request["path"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
    let segments: Vec<&str> = path.split('/').filter(|part| !part.is_empty()).collect();
    let response = match (method, segments.as_slice()) {
        ("GET", ["polls"]) => open_polls()?,
        ("POST", ["polls", slug, "vote"]) => vote(slug, &request)?,
        ("GET", ["polls", slug, "results"]) => results(slug)?,
        (_, ["polls"] | ["polls", _, "vote" | "results"]) => fail(405, "Method not allowed"),
        _ => fail(404, "Not Found"),
    };
    Ok(Json(response))
}
```

The request is `{ method, path, query, headers, body, actor }`, with `body` as a string you parse yourself and `query` as the raw query string. The answer is `{ status, headers?, body }`. Nothing shapes it for you: to keep a Strapi frontend working, answer `{ "data": … }` and, on errors, `{ "data": null, "error": { "status", "name", "message", "details" } }`, as the example’s `ok` and `fail` helpers do.

The vote route checks, in order: a valid body, a poll with that slug, `estado` is `abierta`, the option is one of `opciones`, and no earlier vote with the same fingerprint. Then it creates the `voto` and answers 201 with the results.

No client address in plugin routes

Plugin routes receive only the `content-type`, `accept`, `user-agent` and `accept-language` headers: no IP address, cookies or `Authorization` value. A Strapi controller that used `ctx.request.ip` for “one vote per visitor” needs another key. The example takes a `fingerprint` from the request body, which the site makes (a random id kept in local storage, or a hash of browser traits). It stops double clicks and casual repeats, not a determined voter. For stronger limits, require a signed-in end user (the `actor`) or put the check in front of Verdin.

Other differences from Strapi routes:

* **Routes are public.** Public access and API token permissions are not applied. `actor` says who is calling: `{ "kind": "public" }`, `{ "kind": "token", "id": … }` or `{ "kind": "user", "id": … }` (an end user; only the id). Refuse what the caller may not do, as a Strapi policy would. An invalid token is refused with a 401 before the plugin runs.
* **One call at a time per plugin.** Calls to a plugin wait for each other, so the check and the create in the vote route cannot interleave on one instance. With several instances they can; the example also stores a `clave` (`<poll>:<fingerprint>`) with `unique: true`, so the database refuses a duplicate that slips through.
* **Rate limits apply**: `[api].public_rate_limit` and `[api].token_rate_limit` count plugin routes like the rest of the content API.
* **Anonymous `GET` answers can be cached** when `[api].cache_ttl_secs` is set. Content writes empty the cache, votes included.
* **Only some response headers are kept**: `content-type`, `cache-control`, `location`, `etag`, `last-modified` and `content-disposition`.

## Services to functions and content calls

[Section titled “Services to functions and content calls”](#services-to-functions-and-content-calls)

A Strapi service is shared code; in a plugin it is an ordinary function in the module. Calls to `strapi.documents(uid)` become `verdin_content` calls, limited by the `read` and `write` capabilities:

| Strapi                                     | `verdin_content`                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `findMany({ filters, sort, populate, … })` | `{ "op": "findMany", "uid", "query": { "filters", "sort", "populate", "pagination", … } }` |
| `findOne({ documentId })`                  | `{ "op": "findOne", "uid", "documentId" }`                                                 |
| `create({ data })`                         | `{ "op": "create", "uid", "data" }`                                                        |
| `update({ documentId, data })`             | `{ "op": "update", "uid", "documentId", "data" }`                                          |
| `delete({ documentId })`                   | `{ "op": "delete", "uid", "documentId" }`                                                  |
| `publish` / `unpublish`                    | `{ "op": "publish" }` / `{ "op": "unpublish" }`                                            |
| `count({ filters })`                       | `findMany` with `"pagination": { "pageSize": 1 }`, then `meta.pagination.total`            |

* **Reads return published versions**, unless the query asks for `"status": "draft"`. A hook that looks up a draft-only product finds nothing, as the example’s error message says.
* **Writes are published** unless the request has `"status": "draft"`, like a REST write.
* **The query follows the REST API’s rules.** `private` attributes cannot be used in filters or `fields`, so the example’s `clave` is not private (the public role has no access to votes, so nobody else reads it).
* **No raw SQL, no `strapi.db.query`.** Everything goes through the Document Service, with its validation, webhooks, history and audit log.
* **No clock without WASI.** Set `wasi = true` in the manifest for the time and random numbers; the example’s job uses the `scheduledAt` it receives instead.

## `bootstrap` to the startup function

[Section titled “bootstrap to the startup function”](#bootstrap-to-the-startup-function)

Strapi projects often set the public role’s permissions in `bootstrap`, so that a fresh database is usable and nothing more is open than needed. Verdin’s startup function does the same with the `public_permissions` capability:

plugin/plugin.toml

```toml
[capabilities]
public_permissions = true


[startup]
function = "startup"
```

plugin/src/lib.rs (abridged)

```rust
#[plugin_fn]
pub fn startup(Json(input): Json<Value>) -> FnResult<Json<Value>> {
    let permissions = json!([
        { "subject": "api::producto", "action": "find" },
        { "subject": "api::producto", "action": "findOne" },
        { "subject": "api::encuesta", "action": "find" },
        { "subject": "api::encuesta", "action": "findOne" },
        { "subject": "api::reserva", "action": "create" },
    ]);
    let result = unsafe {
        verdin_public_permissions(Json(json!({ "op": "set", "permissions": permissions })))?
    }
    .0;
    if let Some(error) = result["error"].as_str() {
        return Ok(Json(json!({ "error": format!("public permissions: {error}") })));
    }
    Ok(Json(json!({})))
}
```

* It runs with `{ "reason": "start" | "enabled" | "settings" }`: when the server starts with the plugin on, when the plugin is switched on, and when its settings change. Make it safe to run again: look up what you seed before creating it.
* `set` **replaces all** the public permissions, so changes made in **Settings → Public access** are undone at the next start. The example has a setting to turn this off.
* It runs in the background on a module instance of its own, with its own time limit (`[startup].timeout_ms`, 30 seconds by default), so a slow seed does not hold up hooks and routes. A failure, or an `{ "error" }` answer, is logged; the plugin stays on.
* With several instances, only those with `[plugins].run_jobs = true` run it.

## Cron tasks to jobs

[Section titled “Cron tasks to jobs”](#cron-tasks-to-jobs)

config/cron-tasks.js

```js
module.exports = {
  closePolls: {
    task: async ({ strapi }) => { /* close polls past cierra_el */ },
    options: { rule: '*/15 * * * *' },
  },
};
```

plugin/plugin.toml

```toml
[[jobs]]
schedule = "*/15 * * * *"
function = "close_polls"
```

The job receives `{ "scheduledAt": "…" }` and, in the example, updates every open poll whose `cierra_el` is earlier. Jobs run in UTC, only while the plugin is on, and only on instances with `[plugins].run_jobs = true`. A run missed while the server was down is not made up.

## Admin widgets

[Section titled “Admin widgets”](#admin-widgets)

A Strapi admin widget is a React component; a Verdin widget is a custom element in the plugin’s `admin/` script, declared in the manifest:

plugin/plugin.toml

```toml
[admin]
script = "index.js"


[[admin.widgets]]
id = "polls"
title = "Open polls"
element = "tienda-polls"
```

The element gets a `context` with `fetch`. The example’s widget calls the plugin’s own `GET /api/plugins/tienda/polls` route. Requests to the content API (plugin routes included) go without the admin’s session, so a route a widget uses must be fine for the public, or accept an API token. Injection zones, custom admin pages and React extensions have no equivalent. See [Admin extension points](/verdin/extending/plugin-reference/#admin-extension-points).

## Custom forms to Forms

[Section titled “Custom forms to Forms”](#custom-forms-to-forms)

A suggestions or contact form in Strapi is usually a custom endpoint (or a content type with a public `create` permission) plus code that emails someone. Do not port it: the built-in [Forms](/verdin/guides/frontend/forms/) feature does all of that without code. Editors define the fields in the admin, the site posts to `POST /api/_forms/{slug}`, and submissions are validated, emailed to the **Notify** addresses and exported as CSV. Forms also have a spam trap and a per-visitor rate limit (10 submissions a minute), which a plugin route cannot do because it does not see the client’s address.

## Policies and middlewares

[Section titled “Policies and middlewares”](#policies-and-middlewares)

Verdin has no hook into the HTTP request pipeline. What it offers instead:

| Strapi                                                          | Verdin                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `is-authenticated`-style policies on REST routes                | Public access, API token permissions and end-user roles. See [Permissions](/verdin/reference/permissions/). Finer rules (an end user editing only their own entries) need a plugin route. |
| A policy on a custom route                                      | Check `actor` in the plugin route.                                                                                                                                                        |
| A rate-limit middleware                                         | `[api].public_rate_limit`, `[api].token_rate_limit` and `[admin].auth_rate_limit`.                                                                                                        |
| A CORS or security-headers middleware                           | `[api].cors_origins`; other response headers at the reverse proxy.                                                                                                                        |
| A middleware that rewrites requests or responses of core routes | Not supported. Use a plugin route for the new behavior, or a reverse proxy.                                                                                                               |
| A policy that refuses some writes                               | A before hook that answers `{ error }`, without knowing the caller.                                                                                                                       |

## Limits to plan around

[Section titled “Limits to plan around”](#limits-to-plan-around)

* **No client address and few headers** in plugin routes (see above).
* **Writes made by plugins skip every plugin’s before hooks**, so rules in before hooks do not apply to them.
* **After hooks fired by a plugin’s own writes run after its call returns**, not inside the write, and hooks that write nest at most 4 levels deep (see [Writes made by plugins](/verdin/extending/plugin-reference/#writes-made-by-plugins)). Do follow-up work that must happen before the response in the code that writes, after `verdin_content` returns.
* **One call at a time per plugin**: a slow route delays that plugin’s hooks. Keep calls short, and watch `verdin_plugin_call_duration_seconds` in the [metrics](/verdin/deploy/monitoring/).
* **Routes are public** and must check `actor`.
* **Verdin 0.11 or later** for the startup function and `verdin_public_permissions`: a module that imports a host function the server lacks does not load at all.

## Checklist

[Section titled “Checklist”](#checklist)

1. Import the project with `verdin import strapi`, then list the code in `src/`: routes, controllers, services, lifecycles, policies, middlewares, `bootstrap`, cron tasks and admin extensions.
2. Drop what Verdin does built in: forms, public permissions set by hand, rate limits, CORS, webhooks, scheduled publishing ([Releases](/verdin/guides/content/releases/)).
3. Write one plugin with the rest, following the example: hooks, routes, a job, a startup function. Give it only the capabilities it needs.
4. Check that hooks writing content do not rely on nesting deeper than 4 levels.
5. Build it, install it under `plugins/`, switch it on in **Settings → Plugins**, and read its log there.
6. Update the frontend: plugin route URLs (`/api/plugins/<name>/…`), fingerprints or end-user sign-in where the code relied on the client’s address, and the [other changes](/verdin/migrate/from-strapi/#frontend-changes) of a migration.

# Upgrading Verdin

> Upgrade a Verdin installation — the binary or the Docker image, the migrations that run on start, and the notable or breaking changes of each minor version.

This page explains how to move a project to a newer Verdin version, and lists what changed between minor versions. Verdin follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) with a 0.x twist: until 1.0, a **minor** release (0.8 → 0.9) may change behaviour, and a **patch** release (0.9.0 → 0.9.1) only fixes and hardens.

## Before you upgrade

[Section titled “Before you upgrade”](#before-you-upgrade)

1. **Read the changelog** from your version to the new one: the [changelog](/verdin/project/changelog/) lists every change, and the [notes below](#upgrade-notes) summarize the ones that need action.
2. **Back up** the database and the media storage (see [Backups](/verdin/deploy/backups/)). Going back to an older version means restoring that backup: older versions do not undo the tables and columns a newer one added.
3. **Try it on a copy** of production if the notes mention behaviour your frontend or editors rely on.

You can skip versions. Migrations are computed from the difference between the database and what the new version expects, not replayed one release at a time, so 0.6 → 0.9 migrates in one run. Read the notes of every version in between.

## Upgrade

[Section titled “Upgrade”](#upgrade)

* Docker

  1. Change the image tag in your Compose file, manifest or `Dockerfile`, for example `ghcr.io/verdin-cms/verdin:0.10` → `ghcr.io/verdin-cms/verdin:0.11`. A minor tag (`0.10`) follows its patch releases; pin a full version (`0.10.0`) to decide when those arrive too.

  2. Pull and restart:

     ```sh
     docker compose pull verdin
     docker compose up -d verdin
     docker compose logs -f verdin
     ```

     The image’s default command, `start --migrate`, applies the new version’s migrations before it serves. Look for `applied migrations` and `verdin listening` in the logs.

* Binary

  1. Download the archive for your platform from the [releases page](https://github.com/Verdin-CMS/verdin/releases), for example `verdin-v0.10.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz`, and check it against the release’s `SHA256SUMS`:

     ```sh
     sha256sum --ignore-missing -c SHA256SUMS
     tar xzf verdin-v0.10.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
     ```

  2. Stop the server, replace the `verdin` binary, and check the version:

     ```sh
     verdin version
     ```

  3. Review and apply the migrations from the project directory:

     ```sh
     verdin migrate plan
     verdin migrate apply
     ```

     Or start with `verdin start --migrate`, which applies the safe steps first.

  4. Start the server as usual (`verdin start`).

## Migrations on start

[Section titled “Migrations on start”](#migrations-on-start)

A new version often adds tables or columns of its own (sessions, settings, new features). `verdin start` compares the database with what the schema and the new version need:

* If they match, it starts.
* If steps are pending, it refuses to start and tells you to run `verdin migrate plan` and `verdin migrate apply`, or to start with `--migrate`.
* `--migrate` applies **safe** steps only. If a step is risky or destructive, the start fails and you apply it yourself with `verdin migrate apply --allow risky` (or `destructive`) after reading the plan.
* On MySQL and MariaDB, where schema changes cannot run in a transaction, an interrupted migration resumes from the failed step on the next `verdin migrate apply`.

With several instances, a rolling upgrade works: the first new instance takes the migration lock and migrates, the others wait for it and find nothing left to do. See [Running several instances](/verdin/deploy/scaling/).

Caution

Upgrade the whole project to one version. Do not keep instances of two minor versions running side by side for longer than a rolling deploy takes.

## Upgrade notes

[Section titled “Upgrade notes”](#upgrade-notes)

Notable and breaking changes per version, oldest last. The [changelog](/verdin/project/changelog/) has the complete list.

### 0.10 → 0.11

[Section titled “0.10 → 0.11”](#010--011)

The migration that runs on start adds one table, `vd_cluster_events`, used only when `[cluster] bus = "database"`.

* **Decimals**: whole `decimal` values are returned as JSON integers (`25`, not `25.0`), as Strapi returns them. Clients that check the JSON type strictly may notice; `[api] decimal_as_string` is unchanged. On SQLite, `sort` and `$gt`/`$lt`/`$between` on decimals now compare numbers instead of text, so results that relied on the old (wrong) order change.
* **`populate=*` on localized types** also returns `localizations`, the document’s other locale versions, as Strapi v5 does. A schema attribute named `localizations` keeps its meaning.
* **Plugins**: after hooks fired by a plugin’s own writes run once its call returns instead of inside the write, and hooks that write nest at most 4 levels deep. Host functions stop at the call’s time limit.
* **Several instances**: set `[cluster] bus = "database"` on every instance so realtime streams, presence, the response cache and the search index follow changes made on the others (see [Scaling](/verdin/deploy/scaling/)).
* **Scripts that read admin lists**: `GET /admin/api/users`, `/roles`, `/api-tokens`, `/webhooks`, `/releases`, `/site/redirects`, `/site/menus`, `/site/forms` and `/deploy/targets` return 25 rows unless you pass `pageSize` (at most 100), with `meta.pagination`, like the lists that were already paged. Walk the pages with `?page=` until `page` reaches `meta.pagination.pageCount`. `/deploy/deployments` pages the same way instead of returning the latest 50; `limit` still works as a deprecated alias of `pageSize`. See [Lists](/verdin/api/admin/#lists).

### 0.9.1 → 0.10

[Section titled “0.9.1 → 0.10”](#091--010)

No database migration. The documentation moved from `docs/` to this site.

* **Webhook consumers of `review-workflows.updateEntryStage`**: `model` is now the singular name (`article`), as in entry events, and the uid moved to `uid`. Read `uid` where you used `model`.
* **Regenerate your TypeScript types** with `verdin types`: `Collections` and `Singles` are type aliases now, which `createClient<VerdinSchema>` needs.
* **Docker**: the image keeps the transformation cache and the search index in `/data` and links `/app/public/uploads` to `/data/uploads`. If you set `VERDIN_UPLOAD__TRANSFORMS__CACHE_DIR` or `VERDIN_SEARCH__DIR` only to work around the read-only `/app`, you can drop them. The image has a `HEALTHCHECK`.
* **CDN**: responses carry the tags of the types they can populate, so purges refresh more of the cache than before; nothing to change.
* Relation fields in the admin panel link entries through a dialog (**Link an entry**) instead of an inline search box.

### 0.9.0 → 0.9.1

[Section titled “0.9.0 → 0.9.1”](#090--091)

A hardening release; upgrading is recommended for every installation. Its migration (one new table, two new columns) runs on start.

* **Behind a reverse proxy, set `[server].trusted_proxies`.** Only listed proxies’ `X-Forwarded-For` is used for the client address; otherwise every client behind the proxy shares one address for rate limits and audit logs.
* **Browser frontends on another origin need `[api].cors_origins`.** 0.9.1 adds CORS to the content API and GraphQL; there was no CORS support before.
* **Reads through relations follow permissions.** `populate`, relation filters and relation sorts reach only the types and fields the caller may read, on every API. Public and token requests that populated types they had no `find` grant on now get less data: grant the missing permissions.
* **SSO is stricter.** Its settings need a Super Admin; `defaultRoles` and `roleMap` cannot grant Super Admin; the provider’s `email_verified` claim must be true (unless `trustUnverifiedEmail`); admins’ second factor applies unless the provider is trusted for it (`providerMfa`); the issuer and token endpoint must be public `https` URLs. Check your SSO sign-ins after upgrading.
* **Super Admins** can only be created, edited, deleted, re-invited or reset by another Super Admin.
* **End-user accounts lock** after repeated wrong passwords, like admin accounts.
* Populated relations return at most 1,000 entries per entry and relation.
* Search indexes are rebuilt on the first start (private component fields are no longer indexed).

### 0.8 → 0.9

[Section titled “0.8 → 0.9”](#08--09)

* The admin list’s search box searches every text field (`_q`) instead of the title.
* New admin permissions `deploy.manage`, `deploy.trigger` and `site.manage`; Editors get `deploy.trigger` and `site.manage`.
* New optional features (realtime, comments and tasks, AI actions, SEO and sitemap, redirects, menus, forms) are off until you switch them on. Metrics need `[metrics].enabled = true`.

### 0.7 → 0.8

[Section titled “0.7 → 0.8”](#07--08)

* **Conditional fields are applied**: a field hidden by its `conditions` is no longer required. Content that relied on such a field being required may now save without it.
* New `password` attribute type; `verdin import strapi` now imports Strapi’s password fields.

### 0.7.0 → 0.7.1

[Section titled “0.7.0 → 0.7.1”](#070--071)

* The plugin runtime moves to Wasmtime 48. Existing plugins keep working without a rebuild.
* Building from source needs Rust 1.95 or later.

### 0.6 → 0.7

[Section titled “0.6 → 0.7”](#06--07)

* **Several instances**: each instance reads settings changed by the others every `[server].sync_interval_secs` (10 s). If you run more than one, set `[plugins].run_jobs = false` on all but one.
* Content that plugins write through the host now goes through the platform’s before-write checks, such as review workflow stages. Plugins’ own before-write hooks are still skipped for these writes, so a plugin cannot trigger itself.

### 0.5 → 0.6

[Section titled “0.5 → 0.6”](#05--06)

* **Audit logs** are on by default and keep entries for `[audit].retention_days` (90). Turn the feature off in **Settings → Features** if you do not want them.

### 0.4 → 0.5

[Section titled “0.4 → 0.5”](#04--05)

* Nothing to change. Plugins are loaded from `[plugins].path` (`plugins/`) and stay off until switched on.

### 0.3 → 0.4

[Section titled “0.3 → 0.4”](#03--04)

* **`auth`, `users` and `connect` are reserved route names**, along with `upload` and `uploads`: rename content types whose API name is one of them before upgrading.

### 0.2 → 0.3

[Section titled “0.2 → 0.3”](#02--03)

* Attribute names follow Strapi’s rule (a letter, then letters, digits and underscores) instead of camelCase only. Two names that map to the same column are refused.
* `regex` options accept JavaScript-like patterns.

### 0.1 → 0.2

[Section titled “0.1 → 0.2”](#01--02)

* Body size limits and timeouts apply per API router; uploads have their own limits (`[upload].max_file_size`).
* Built-in roles of existing installations receive the new permissions once.

# Changelog

All notable changes to Verdin are documented here. The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and the project uses [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) (0.x: minor versions may break).

## \[Unreleased]

[Section titled “\[Unreleased\]”](#unreleased)

Operations at scale, and the fixes found by moving a real Strapi 5.55 project to Verdin. The migration that runs on start adds one table (`vd_cluster_events`). See the [upgrade notes](https://verdin-cms.github.io/verdin/migrate/upgrading/#010--011).

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added)

* **Shared event bus**: `[cluster] bus = "database"` carries realtime events, presence, response cache invalidation, search index updates and transform cache purges between instances, through `vd_cluster_events`, with `LISTEN/NOTIFY` on PostgreSQL and polling (`poll_interval_ms`) on MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite. A single instance keeps the in-process path and writes nothing. New metric `verdin_cluster_events_total`.
* **Observability**: `[telemetry]` exports OpenTelemetry traces over OTLP/HTTP (request spans that join a caller’s `traceparent`, and a span per SQL statement without bound values) and reports panics and 5xx responses to Sentry; both off by default, with the standard `OTEL_*` and `SENTRY_*` variables. A Grafana dashboard in `docker/grafana/verdin.json`.
* **Plugins**: a `[startup]` function run when the plugin starts, is switched on or its settings change (Strapi’s `bootstrap`), on the instances that run jobs; the `public_permissions` capability and `verdin_public_permissions` host function; call durations and failures in `verdin_plugin_call_duration_seconds` and `verdin_plugin_call_errors_total`.
* **Strapi i18n responses**: `localizations` can be populated on localized types (REST and GraphQL), and `GET /api/i18n/locales` lists the locales with Strapi’s shape, behind a `find` permission on `plugin::i18n.locale`. `verdin import strapi` maps that permission; `@verdin/client` has `locales()`.
* **Porting Strapi custom code**: a guide and an example plugin (`examples/strapi-port`) with a before hook, routes, a scheduled job, a startup function and a dashboard widget.
* **Packaging**: `.deb` packages for amd64 and arm64 with a systemd unit, an install script (`install.sh`, checksum-verified), `cargo binstall` metadata, Homebrew and winget release jobs (skipped without their secrets), a Helm chart, a production Compose recipe with PostgreSQL and Caddy, one-click deploy files for Render, DigitalOcean, Railway, Fly and Coolify, and a playground container that resets every hour.
* **Docs hosting**: the site’s address is one `SITE_URL` variable, and pull requests get a preview under `pr-preview/pr-N/`.
* Admin API: `?page=&pageSize=` on users, roles, API tokens, webhooks, releases, redirects (with `search`), menus, forms, deploy targets and deployments; the admin panel pages those lists.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed)

* Whole `decimal` values are returned as JSON integers (`25`, not `25.0`), as in Strapi.
* The admin lists above return 25 rows by default instead of every row, and deployments 25 instead of 50 (`limit` is a deprecated alias of `pageSize`).
* After hooks fired by a plugin’s own writes run once its call returns, nesting at most 4 levels deep.
* The site is published from the `gh-pages` branch.

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed)

* **SQLite**: `decimal` sorts and `$gt`/`$lt`/`$between` filters compared text, so `sort=price:desc` gave `8, 6, 25, 12, 10`; they compare numbers now.
* **SQLite**: writers queue in arrival order instead of retrying on `busy_timeout`. With 20 concurrent writers the p99 went from about 88 ms to 11 ms and throughput from about 2 300 to 3 100 requests per second.
* A plugin route or job writing a type the same plugin has after hooks on hung the plugin and every write to that type, and the server could not be stopped: host functions now stop at the call’s time limit, and shutdown gives requests, the database and background tasks a bounded grace period.
* Releases older than the latest 500 could not be found by id or from their entries.

## \[0.10.0] - 2026-09-29

[Section titled “\[0.10.0\] - 2026-09-29”](#0100---2026-09-29)

Modern documentation and admin polish. The documentation moved from `docs/` to a site of its own, rewritten and checked against the code; the admin panel’s largest screens were split up and gained accessibility and tests. No database migration.

### Documentation

[Section titled “Documentation”](#documentation)

* **A documentation site**, published to GitHub Pages on every push to `main` (<https://verdin-cms.github.io/verdin/>): Get started (quickstart, Astro and Next.js tutorials), Concepts, Guides, Extending, API reference, Reference, Deploy & operate, Migrate & upgrade and Internals. It has its own look, code tabs, diagrams, an API playground on the example project, Open Graph cards, `llms.txt`, and pages in 18 languages.
* The permissions reference is generated from the code, and CI checks that the command line reference covers every command and flag.
* The user guides and the design document that were in `docs/` are pages of the site now; `docs/` keeps the roadmap and the translation guide. `SECURITY.md` says how to report a vulnerability.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-1)

* `verdin healthcheck` asks `/_health` on the loopback interface; the Docker image uses it as its `HEALTHCHECK`.
* GraphQL: localized types have a `locale` field, and `delete…` mutations take `locale`.
* Admin panel: page titles for every screen, a “Skip to content” link, focus moved to the page heading after navigation (announced to screen readers), subtle view transitions (off with reduced motion), one entry picker for relations, polymorphic relations and menu items, pagination controls on audit logs, webhook deliveries, end users and form submissions, and the rich-text editors loaded only when a field needs them.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-1)

* **CDN**: content API responses carry the cache tags of every type they can populate, so purging a related type also refreshes them.
* **Docker image**: uploads (`/app/public/uploads` links to `/data/uploads`), the image transformation cache and the search index live in `/data`, so the S3 upload provider can be set with environment variables alone.
* **Webhooks**: `review-workflows.updateEntryStage` carries the singular name in `model` and the uid in `uid`, like entry events (`model` held the uid).
* Relation fields link entries through a dialog (**Link an entry**) that searches every text field of the target type, in the entry’s locale for localized targets.
* `verdin types` emits `Collections` and `Singles` as type aliases, so `createClient<VerdinSchema>` type-checks; regenerate your types.
* `verdin new` adds `public/uploads/` to the project’s `.gitignore`.
* The admin panel’s editor, content-type builder, content list and media library were split into smaller components with one state service each, and settings pages load through Angular resources; behaviour is unchanged.

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-1)

* Two-factor sign-ins are audited once the second factor is accepted, with the admin (the password step was recorded without one).
* Invitations say they were not emailed when the email provider is `log`.
* Plugin widgets’ `context.fetch` sends content API requests without the admin session, which the content API refused.
* The end-user roles page says that signed-in users get only their role’s permissions.

## \[0.9.1] - 2026-09-29

[Section titled “\[0.9.1\] - 2026-09-29”](#091---2026-09-29)

A hardening release from a full audit of 0.9.0. Upgrading is recommended for every installation; its migration (one table, two columns) runs on start.

### Security

[Section titled “Security”](#security)

* **Super Admins**: only a Super Admin can create, edit, delete, re-invite or reset the second factor of a Super Admin, or grant that role. Re-inviting an account that has signed in is refused, and accepting an invitation goes through the second factor.
* **SSO**: its settings need a Super Admin; `defaultRoles` and `roleMap` cannot grant Super Admin; the provider’s `email_verified` must be true (unless `trustUnverifiedEmail`); the second factor applies unless the provider is trusted for it (`providerMfa`); the issuer and token endpoint must be public `https` URLs.
* **Rights on related types**: `populate`, relation filters and relation sorts reach only the types (and fields) the caller may read, on REST, GraphQL, MCP and the admin API; polymorphic relations and references skip the others.
* **History** applies per-locale permissions.
* **Sign-in**: failed attempts count across the password and second-factor steps and are counted atomically, so a correct password no longer resets the counter; password confirmations are limited too. End users’ accounts now lock after repeated wrong passwords as well (`failed_logins`, `locked_until` on `vd_users`).
* **Rate limits behind proxies**: `[server] trusted_proxies` names the reverse proxies whose `X-Forwarded-For` is trusted; unknown bearer tokens are limited per address.
* **Passkeys**: spent challenges are kept in the database (`vd_spent_challenges`), so a challenge is answered once across instances; RSA keys must have 2048 to 8192 bits and a sane exponent.
* TOTP secrets are sealed with a MAC (older secrets still open); form submitters’ IPs are hashed with a key derived from `VERDIN_TOKEN_PEPPER`; request logs hide secret-looking query parameters and deploy callback secrets; webhooks and fetches refuse IPv6 addresses that embed private IPv4 ones (`::a.b.c.d`, 6to4, Teredo, `fec0::/10`).
* Private fields of components are no longer indexed by search (indexes are rebuilt on start).

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-2)

* `[api] cors_origins`: browser origins allowed to call the content API and GraphQL (`["*"]` for any). There was no CORS support before.
* `beforeDiscardDraft` plugin hook; discarding a draft runs the before hooks.
* Expired sessions, one-time links and passkey challenges are pruned daily.
* Admin panel: leaving an entry or the content-type builder with unsaved changes asks first (also on locale switches, remote-change reloads and closing the tab); unpublishing and discarding a draft ask for confirmation; pages the admin may not open redirect home instead of loading forever; the users, tokens, roles and public permissions pages show loading and error states with a retry.

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-2)

* JSON answers over 4 MB are served without an ETag instead of failing.
* Populated relations return at most 1000 entries per entry and relation; `count` populates read no fields.
* The admin export reads only the documents it exports; the sitemap is built at most every ten minutes.
* “Where used” no longer holds a write lock on SQLite.
* Huge `pagination[page]`/`pagination[start]` values give an empty page instead of an error.
* Mentions only notify admins who may read the entry (own-entries grants included); imports report database errors instead of a refusal.

## \[0.9.0] - 2026-09-29

[Section titled “\[0.9.0\] - 2026-09-29”](#090---2026-09-29)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-3)

* **Realtime events** over Server-Sent Events: `GET /api/_events` (the `realtime` feature) and `GET /admin/api/events`, each filtered by what the subscriber may read, and **presence** on entries (`/admin/api/presence`) with a soft lock for the first editor. See [Realtime events](https://verdin-cms.github.io/verdin/guides/frontend/realtime/).
* **Prometheus metrics** at `/_metrics` (`[metrics]`): requests and latency by area, webhook queue, realtime streams, uptime.
* **Cross-field validations**: `validations: [{ rule, message, field }]` in a content type, JSON Logic rules checked with `required` (`endDate >= startDate`). JSON Logic comparisons now also order strings (ISO dates), and arithmetic, `min`, `max` and `cat` are supported.
* **Where used**: `GET /admin/api/content/:uid/:documentId/usage` and `GET /admin/api/upload/files/:id/usage` list the versions referencing an entry (relations, polymorphic relations, relations in components) or a file (media fields and components, image blocks, rich text URLs), filtered by the admin’s permissions.
* **Image transformations** at `/uploads/<file>?preset=…` or signed `?w=&h=&fit=&format=&q=&s=` (`[upload.transforms]`, `VERDIN_IMAGE_SECRET`): cover crops around the focal point, JPEG/PNG/WebP output, a disk cache dropped when the file changes.
* **Full-text search** with `_q` on the content and admin APIs: `$containsi` over the text fields (Strapi’s behaviour), or, with `[search] enabled = true`, a Tantivy index that ranks results, ignores accents and matches the last word as a prefix.
* **Two-factor authentication for admins**: TOTP and passkeys (WebAuthn: ES256, EdDSA, RS256) with single-use recovery codes, a two-step sign-in, and roles that require it (`requireTwoFactor`).
* **CSV/JSON import and export** per content type in the admin API, with column mapping, upserts by `documentId` and a dry run that validates every row without writing.
* **Comments and tasks** on entries and fields (the `comments` feature): threads with @mentions and resolution, tasks with an assignee and due date, email notifications.
* **Deploys and CDN purges**: build hook targets behind a “Deploy” button with a provider status callback (`deploy.manage`, `deploy.trigger`), and `[cdn]` purges by cache tag on Cloudflare, Fastly or a webhook when content changes publicly.
* **Visual editing**: source maps hidden in the text of authenticated reads that send `X-Verdin-Stega: true`, and an overlay script (`/admin/api/visual-editing.js`) that jumps from the site to the field. See [Visual editing](https://verdin-cms.github.io/verdin/guides/frontend/visual-editing/).
* **AI actions** (the `ai` feature, off by default, and `[ai]`): translate an entry to another locale, alt text for images, summaries and SEO suggestions, with Anthropic, OpenAI or any OpenAI-compatible server.
* **Site features** (see [Site features](https://verdin-cms.github.io/verdin/guides/frontend/seo-and-sitemap/)): SEO settings with `/sitemap.xml` and a suggested `shared.seo` component, redirects for frontends (`/api/_redirects`), navigation menus with resolved entry links (`/api/_menus/{slug}`) and forms with validated, rate-limited submissions and email notifications (`/api/_forms/{slug}`). New admin permission `site.manage`.
* **Admin panel**: two-step sign-in with codes and passkeys, and a two-factor section in the profile; comments, tasks and presence in the editor, live list updates and a “My tasks” widget; “Used in” in the editor and the media library with delete warnings; CSV/JSON import (with a checked dry run) and export from the lists, and full-text search in them; AI translation, SEO, summary and alt text suggestions; visual editing from the preview; editable polymorphic relations in the editor and the builder; Settings → Deployments with a Deploy button, and pages for redirects, menus, forms and the SEO settings.
* New admin permissions `deploy.manage`, `deploy.trigger` and `site.manage` (Editors get `deploy.trigger` and `site.manage`).

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-2)

* The admin content list’s search box searches every text field (`_q`) instead of the title.

## \[0.8.0] - 2026-09-28

[Section titled “\[0.8.0\] - 2026-09-28”](#080---2026-09-28)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-4)

* **`password` attributes**: hashed with Argon2id on write and never returned, filtered or sorted. `verdin import strapi` imports them, keeping Strapi’s bcrypt hashes.
* Webhook events `releases.publish` and `review-workflows.updateEntryStage`.
* REST query options from Strapi v5: `populate[tags][count]=true`, `hasPublishedVersion=true|false`, sorting by a to-one relation’s field (`sort=author.name:asc`), filters on repeatable components (`filters[links][url][$contains]=…`) and on dynamic zones by `__component`.
* **Admin accounts**: invite admins without setting a password (`POST /users` without `password` returns `meta.inviteUrl` and emails it), accept the invitation, reset a forgotten password by email, edit one’s own profile (`/users/me`), list and sign out one’s sessions (`/auth/sessions`), and regenerate API tokens (`POST /api-tokens/{id}/regenerate`).
* **End users**: refresh tokens (`jwtManagement: "refresh"`, `POST /api/auth/refresh` and `/api/auth/logout`), the `/api/users` routes with role permissions on `plugin::users-permissions.user`, OAuth presets for Microsoft, Discord, Facebook, GitLab and LinkedIn, and HTML email templates.
* **Admin branding** in `[admin.branding]`: title, logo, favicon, accent color and text overrides per language.
* **Permissions per locale**: admin content permissions take an optional `locales` list (`{ "action": "content.update", "subject": "api::article", "locales": ["fr"] }`).
* **Conditional fields** (Strapi 5.17’s `conditions.visible`, JSON Logic): hidden fields are not required.
* **Edit view layout** per content type (`/admin/api/content-types/{uid}/edit-view`, permission `views.manage`): field order and widths, labels, descriptions, placeholders, read-only fields and the field that names related entries.
* **GraphQL**: disable queries or mutations per content type (the feature’s `disabled` setting, like Strapi’s shadow CRUD), and root fields resolved by plugins (`[[graphql]]` in `plugin.toml`).
* **Media library**: replace a file keeping its id and links (`POST /admin/api/upload/files/{id}/replace`, and `POST /api/upload?id=` with a file, as in Strapi), upload from a URL (`POST /admin/api/upload/from-url`, public addresses only unless private networks are allowed), and `[upload].max_original_size` to scale down large originals.
* **MCP server** (the `mcp` feature): content tools for AI agents at `/mcp` (Streamable HTTP), authorized like the content API. See [MCP server](https://verdin-cms.github.io/verdin/guides/integrations/mcp/).
* **Backups**: `verdin export <file.tar.gz>` and `verdin import verdin <file.tar.gz>` move a project’s schema, locales, media and every version of its entries. See [Backups](https://verdin-cms.github.io/verdin/deploy/backups/).
* Duplicate entries: `POST /admin/api/content/{uid}/{documentId}/clone` creates a draft with the entry’s content. Unique and uid fields and one-to-one / one-to-many relations are left out and listed in `meta.leftOut`.
* **Polymorphic relations**: `morphToOne` and `morphToMany` link documents of any content type (`{ "__type": uid, "documentId": id }`), and `morphOne` / `morphMany` read them from the other side. They are populated in REST and GraphQL (as JSON), copied on publish, kept by history, duplicates and `verdin export`, and imported from Strapi.
* **Admin panel**: a filter builder in the content lists, drag-and-drop relations with editing in a side sheet, a side-by-side live preview with device widths, duplicate from the list and the editor, the edit view configurator, conditional fields in the editor and the builder, crop, replace, upload from URL and PDF preview in the media library, the profile page with sessions, invitations and password resets, and settings for the MCP server and GraphQL’s disabled operations.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-3)

* The HTTP API tests of `verdin-api` build into one binary, which saves about 2.7 GB in `target/` per build.

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-3)

* Tables with foreign keys are created (and dropped) in dependency order at any depth, which PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB need.

## \[0.7.1] - 2026-09-28

[Section titled “\[0.7.1\] - 2026-09-28”](#071---2026-09-28)

### Security

[Section titled “Security”](#security-1)

* The plugin runtime moves from Wasmtime 43 to Wasmtime 48 (LTS). This fixes RUSTSEC-2026-0222 (stores could mix up type indices between engines) and RUSTSEC-2026-0269 (filesystem sandbox escape through trailing slashes), and drops the unmaintained crates that came with Wasmtime 43. No Extism release ships Wasmtime 48 yet, so Extism comes from its main branch, pinned to a commit. Existing plugins keep working without a rebuild.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-4)

* The minimum Rust version is now 1.95, which Wasmtime 48 requires.

## \[0.7.0] - 2026-09-28

[Section titled “\[0.7.0\] - 2026-09-28”](#070---2026-09-28)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-5)

* **Review workflows** (the `review` feature, permission `workflows.manage`). Stages per content type, with the roles allowed to move entries into each stage. Entries can be assigned to an admin. A workflow can also require a stage to publish, which is enforced on every API. The admin shows stages in the editor and the list, and the entries assigned to you on the home page. See [Review workflows](https://verdin-cms.github.io/verdin/guides/content/review-workflows/).
* **Right-to-left admin languages**: Arabic, Hebrew and Persian (18 languages in all).
* **Documentation site** in `site/` (Astro Starlight), built from `docs/`, with a configuration reference and an API reference generated from OpenAPI.
* **Several instances.** Each instance reads the settings changed by the others every `[server].sync_interval_secs`. Set `[plugins].run_jobs = false` on all instances but one. Each day’s digest is claimed in the database, so it is sent once. See [Running several instances](https://verdin-cms.github.io/verdin/deploy/scaling/).

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-4)

* Schemas from Strapi 5.17+ with conditional fields (`conditions`) failed to load. The conditions are now kept, but the admin does not apply them yet.
* Plugins writing content through the host skipped every before-write hook. They now skip only the plugins’ own hooks.

## \[0.6.0] - 2026-09-28

[Section titled “\[0.6.0\] - 2026-09-28”](#060---2026-09-28)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-6)

* **SSO for admins** (the `sso` feature): sign-in through OpenID Connect providers with PKCE, a signed state and a nonce. Accounts can be created on first sign-in, with roles mapped from a groups claim. Client secrets come from `VERDIN_SSO_<ID>_SECRET`. See [Single sign-on](https://verdin-cms.github.io/verdin/guides/auth/sso/).
* **Audit logs** (the `audit` feature, on by default, permission `audit.read`). They record content and media changes from every API, admin actions and sign-ins, and keep them for `[audit].retention_days`. Read them in `GET /admin/api/audit-logs` with filters.
* **Releases** (the `releases` feature, permission `releases.manage`): entries published or unpublished together, now or at a scheduled date, with a result for each action.
* **Preview** (the `preview` feature): URL templates per content type, and signed short-lived tokens (`x-verdin-preview`) that read one draft through the content API.
* **Plugin settings forms**: plugins declare `[[settings]]` fields (types, options, defaults, bounds). The admin shows a form, and the server validates the values.
* **Unseen digest**: an opt-in daily email of unseen changes (preference `digest: "daily"`), sent at `[digest].hour_utc`.

See [Audit logs](https://verdin-cms.github.io/verdin/guides/content/audit-logs/) for audit logs, releases, preview and the digest.

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-5)

* Settings → Features listed plugins as “planned for 0.5” although they shipped.

## \[0.5.0] - 2026-09-25

[Section titled “\[0.5.0\] - 2026-09-25”](#050---2026-09-25)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-7)

* **WASM plugins** (Extism): before/after write hooks (change or refuse data), routes under `/api/plugins/{name}`, cron jobs, key-value storage, settings and logs; capabilities per plugin (content types read/written, HTTP hosts, storage) and time and memory limits; Settings → Plugins (`plugins.manage`). See [Plugins](https://verdin-cms.github.io/verdin/extending/plugins/).
* **Plugin widgets and custom fields**: Web Components shipped by plugins, loaded by the admin; attributes with `customField: "plugin::{plugin}.{field}"` (Strapi-compatible; kept by `verdin import strapi`).
* Chart widgets (entries created and published per day or week, `GET /admin/api/content/{uid}/stats`).
* Unseen badges in the sidebar (`GET /admin/api/engagement/unseen`).
* Document Service before-write hooks (`DocumentHook`).

## \[0.4.0] - 2026-09-25

[Section titled “\[0.4.0\] - 2026-09-25”](#040---2026-09-25)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-8)

* **End users** (the `users` feature, Settings → End users): Strapi v5 compatible `/api/auth/local/register`, `/api/auth/local`, email confirmation, forgot/reset/change password and `/api/users/me`; roles with content API grants; JWTs revoked on password change and block; OAuth sign-in (GitHub, Google, any OAuth 2 provider) with signed, cookie-bound state; accounts, roles and settings in the admin (`endusers.manage`). See [End users](https://verdin-cms.github.io/verdin/guides/auth/end-users/).
* **Email** (`[email]`): SMTP, Resend, Postmark and a log provider; secrets from the environment; test emails from Settings → Features. Mailpit in the development compose file.
* Content API traffic controls: rate limits per IP (`[api].public_rate_limit`) and per token or end user (`[api].token_rate_limit`), `ETag`s with `304 Not Modified`, and an optional in-memory cache of anonymous reads (`[api].cache_ttl_secs`) emptied on every change.
* `verdin import strapi` imports end users (bcrypt passwords keep working), custom roles and the public/authenticated permissions.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-5)

* `auth`, `users` and `connect` are reserved route names for content types.

## \[0.3.0] - 2026-09-25

[Section titled “\[0.3.0\] - 2026-09-25”](#030---2026-09-25)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-9)

* **Webhooks** (Settings → Webhooks): entry and media events, per content type filters, custom headers, HMAC-SHA256 signatures, a durable delivery queue with retries and backoff, a delivery log with manual retry, test deliveries, SSRF protection in production (`[webhooks]` settings); `webhooks.manage` permission. See [Webhooks](https://verdin-cms.github.io/verdin/guides/integrations/webhooks/).
* **Content history**: a version of the document after every create, save, publish, unpublish and discarded draft, from any API. Browse the versions from the editor and restore one as the draft: fields that no longer exist are skipped, and references to deleted entries or files are dropped and reported. Newest `[history].max_versions` versions (50) are kept per document.
* **Content internationalization**: locales (Settings → Internationalization, `locales.manage`), localized content types and shared fields (`pluginOptions.i18n.localized`), one version per locale with its own draft and published version, `?locale=` on the REST and admin APIs and a `locale` argument in GraphQL, locale-aware relations and filters, a locale switcher and “fill from another locale” in the editor. See [docs/i18n.md](https://verdin-cms.github.io/verdin/guides/content/localizing-content/).
* **`verdin import strapi`**: imports a Strapi v4/v5 export (`strapi export --no-encrypt`, `.tar.gz`, `.tar` or directory): schema files, locales, media library, entries (drafts, published versions, locales), relations and media, including inside components; writes a Strapi → Verdin id map. See [Migrating from Strapi](https://verdin-cms.github.io/verdin/migrate/from-strapi/).
* Admin: bulk publish, unpublish and delete from the content list, with progress and a summary of failures.
* Admin: list view settings per content type and user (visible columns and their order, default sort and page size).

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-6)

* Attribute names follow Strapi’s rule (a letter, then letters, digits and underscores: `kit_man`, `SEO`) instead of camelCase only; names that map to the same column are refused.
* `regex` options accept JavaScript-like patterns (look-around, backreferences), with a backtracking limit.

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-6)

* Writes made through GraphQL did not reach document listeners (for example “not seen yet” marks).

## \[0.2.0] - 2026-09-25

[Section titled “\[0.2.0\] - 2026-09-25”](#020---2026-09-25)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-10)

* **Media library**: `media` attribute type (single or multiple, `allowedTypes`), uploads with MIME sniffing and responsive image formats, folders, focal points, local and S3-compatible storage (AWS, R2, B2, RustFS), Strapi-compatible `/api/upload` routes and `plugin::upload` grants, admin media permissions.
* Admin: media library page (folders, drag & drop uploads with progress, grid/list views, search and type filters, bulk move/delete, file details with focal point, alt text and caption), media picker and media fields in the editor, media field type in the builder, media permissions in roles, and a media library row in public access and API tokens.
* **Settings → Features**: switch optional features on and off at runtime (the app is rebuilt in place, no restart), with the roadmap’s upcoming features listed; `features.manage` permission.
