See [Monitoring](/verdin/deploy/monitoring/).

## `verdin secrets`

[Section titled “verdin secrets”](#verdin-secrets)

Terminal

```text
verdin secrets
```

Prints a fresh `VERDIN_ADMIN_JWT_SECRET` and `VERDIN_TOKEN_PEPPER`, ready for a `.env` file or your platform’s secret store. It reads no project.

Changing `VERDIN_ADMIN_JWT_SECRET` voids the short-lived access tokens of admins and end users, open preview links and OAuth sign-ins in progress; the admin panel and clients that use refresh tokens get new ones by themselves. Changing `VERDIN_TOKEN_PEPPER` invalidates stored tokens (API tokens among them), so keep it once in use.

## `verdin version`

[Section titled “verdin version”](#verdin-version)

Terminal

```text
verdin version
```

Prints `verdin` and the version, like `verdin --version`.

# Configuration reference

> Every section and key of verdin.toml, with defaults, and the environment variables Verdin reads.

Configuration is layered: **built-in defaults ← `verdin.toml` ← environment**. The file is optional; every key has a default. Unknown keys are rejected, so a typo fails at start instead of being ignored.

* Override any key with `VERDIN_<SECTION>__<KEY>` (two underscores), for example `VERDIN_SERVER__PORT=8080` or `VERDIN_ADMIN__SECURE_COOKIES=false`. Nested tables take one more `__`: `VERDIN_ADMIN__BRANDING__TITLE=ACME`. Unknown keys are rejected here too, so any variable that starts with `VERDIN_` and contains `__` must name a real key.
* `VERDIN_DATABASE_URL` is a shorthand for `database.url`.
* The file is `verdin.toml` in the working directory, or the path given with `-c, --config` or `VERDIN_CONFIG`. Relative paths in it (schema, plugins, uploads, SQLite files) are resolved against the file’s directory.
* A `.env` file next to the configuration is loaded first; variables already set in the environment win.

Secrets are never read from `verdin.toml`; see [Environment variables](#environment-variables).

## `[server]`

[Section titled “\[server\]”](#server)

| Key                    | Default     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`                 | `"0.0.0.0"` | Address to listen on.                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `port`                 | `1337`      | Port to listen on.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `public_url`           | unset       | Where browsers reach the server, e.g. `"https://cms.example.com"`. Used for links in emails and SSO callbacks; defaults to `http://localhost:{port}`.                                                    |
| `body_limit`           | `"1mb"`     | Largest request body of regular API requests (uploads have their own limit). A number of bytes or a string with `b`, `kb`, `mb` or `gb`.                                                                 |
| `request_timeout_secs` | `30`        | Time limit of regular API requests.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `sync_interval_secs`   | `10`        | How often to pick up settings changed by other instances (features, plugin switches, locales, review workflows); `0` turns it off (a single instance).                                                   |
| `trusted_proxies`      | `[]`        | Reverse proxies (IPs or CIDR ranges, e.g. `["10.0.0.0/8"]`) whose `X-Forwarded-For` names the client. Rate limits and audit logs use that address; without it, every client behind the proxy shares one. |

## `[database]`

[Section titled “\[database\]”](#database)

| Key        | Default | Description                                                                                                                           |
| ---------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `url`      | unset   | Connection URL: `postgres://…`, `mysql://…` (MySQL and MariaDB) or `sqlite://…`. Required; usually set through `VERDIN_DATABASE_URL`. |
| `pool_max` | `10`    | Maximum connections in the pool.                                                                                                      |

## `[schema]`

[Section titled “\[schema\]”](#schema)

| Key    | Default    | Description                                           |
| ------ | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `path` | `"schema"` | Schema directory, relative to the configuration file. |

## `[api]`

[Section titled “\[api\]”](#api)

| Key                 | Default  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `prefix`            | `"/api"` | Path the content API is served under. Must start with `/` and not end with one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `default_page_size` | `25`     | Page size when a request sets none. Between 1 and `max_page_size`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `max_page_size`     | `100`    | Largest page size a request may ask for.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `decimal_as_string` | `false`  | Serialize decimals as strings (exact) instead of numbers (Strapi-compatible).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `public_rate_limit` | `0`      | Requests per minute and client IP without a token (`0`: unlimited).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `token_rate_limit`  | `0`      | Requests per minute and API token or end user (`0`: unlimited).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `cache_ttl_secs`    | `0`      | Keep anonymous reads in memory this long (`0`: no cache); changes empty the cache.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `cache_entries`     | `1000`   | Maximum number of cached responses.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `cors_origins`      | `[]`     | Browser origins allowed to call the content API and GraphQL from another site (`["https://www.example.com"]`: scheme, host and port, no path), or `["*"]` for any (alone: `*` cannot be combined with origins). Empty: only same-origin pages can call them from a browser. The admin API never takes cross-origin calls. |

## `[admin]`

[Section titled “\[admin\]”](#admin)

| Key               | Default    | Description                                                                                                                |
| ----------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `path`            | `"/admin"` | Path the admin panel is served under; its API lives at `{path}/api`.                                                       |
| `secure_cookies`  | unset      | Mark the refresh cookie `Secure`. Unset means yes in `verdin start` and no in `verdin dev` (plain-HTTP local development). |
| `auth_rate_limit` | `20`       | Login, registration and refresh attempts per client IP per minute.                                                         |
| `assets_dir`      | unset      | Serve the admin panel from this directory (relative to the configuration file) instead of the copy embedded in the binary. |

### `[admin.branding]`

[Section titled “\[admin.branding\]”](#adminbranding)

| Key            | Default    | Description                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`        | `"Verdin"` | Shown in the sidebar, on the sign-in page and in the browser tab.                                                                                                                   |
| `logo`         | unset      | Image file (SVG, PNG, WebP), relative to the configuration file.                                                                                                                    |
| `favicon`      | unset      | Icon file (ICO, PNG, SVG), relative to the configuration file.                                                                                                                      |
| `accent`       | unset      | `#rrggbb` color of buttons, links and focus rings.                                                                                                                                  |
| `translations` | `{}`       | Admin texts replaced per language, for example `[admin.branding.translations.en]` with `"auth.login.title" = "Welcome to ACME"`. The keys are those of `admin/public/i18n/en.json`. |

## `[upload]`

[Section titled “\[upload\]”](#upload)

| Key                    | Default                                      | Description                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `provider`             | `{ name = "local", dir = "public/uploads" }` | Where files are stored; see below.                                                                                                                                 |
| `max_file_size`        | `209715200`                                  | Largest accepted file, in bytes (200 MB).                                                                                                                          |
| `responsive_formats`   | `true`                                       | Generate responsive formats for raster images.                                                                                                                     |
| `breakpoints`          | large 1000, medium 750, small 500            | Responsive formats as `{ name, width }` tables (Strapi’s `breakpoints`). Formats wider than the image are skipped.                                                 |
| `max_image_megapixels` | `100`                                        | Decoding limit against decompression bombs, in megapixels.                                                                                                         |
| `max_original_size`    | unset                                        | Raster originals larger than this many pixels (either side) are scaled down on upload, which also drops their metadata (EXIF, GPS). Unset keeps originals as sent. |

```toml
[upload]
breakpoints = [{ name = "large", width = 1000 }, { name = "small", width = 500 }]
```

### Local provider

[Section titled “Local provider”](#local-provider)

Files under `dir` (relative to the project), served by Verdin at `/uploads`.

```toml
[upload]
provider = { name = "local", dir = "public/uploads" }
```

### `[upload.transforms]`

[Section titled “\[upload.transforms\]”](#uploadtransforms)

Image transformations of local files: `/uploads/<file>?preset=thumb`, or `?w=&h=&fit=&format=&q=` with a signature. Renderings are cached on disk and dropped when the file changes (its focal point included). Cover crops keep the file’s focal point in view; images are never enlarged. JPEG, PNG, WebP, TIFF and BMP can be transformed (not GIFs, which may be animated).

| Key               | Default               | Description                                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `enabled`         | `true`                | Serve transformations.                                                                                             |
| `presets`         | `{}`                  | Named transformations, always allowed: `{ w, h, fit, format, q }`.                                                 |
| `allow_arbitrary` | `false`               | Accept any parameters without a signature. Each distinct URL is rendered and cached, so only for trusted networks. |
| `max_size`        | `4096`                | Largest `w` or `h`, in pixels.                                                                                     |
| `cache_dir`       | `".cache/transforms"` | Where renderings are kept (relative to the project; safe to delete).                                               |

Parameters: `w`, `h` (pixels), `fit` (`cover`, the default, crops to the box; `inside` fits within it; `fill` stretches), `format` (`jpeg`, `png`, `webp`; WebP output is lossless) and `q` (JPEG quality, 1–100, default 80).

```toml
[upload.transforms.presets]
thumb = { w = 300, h = 300 }
hero = { w = 1600, h = 600, format = "webp" }
```

**Signed URLs.** With `VERDIN_IMAGE_SECRET` set, `s` is the hex HMAC-SHA256 of `<file>?<canonical query>`, where the canonical query lists the non-default parameters sorted by name (`fit`, `format`, `h`, `q`, `w`; `fit=cover` omitted):

```js
import { createHmac } from 'node:crypto';
const s = createHmac('sha256', process.env.VERDIN_IMAGE_SECRET)
  .update('photo_1a2b.jpg?format=webp&w=800')
  .digest('hex');
const url = `/uploads/photo_1a2b.jpg?format=webp&w=800&s=${s}`;
```

### S3 provider

[Section titled “S3 provider”](#s3-provider)

Any S3-compatible service (AWS, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, Backblaze B2…). Credentials come from the standard `AWS_*` environment variables (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`).

| Key          | Default  | Description                                                                              |
| ------------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bucket`     | required | Bucket name.                                                                             |
| `region`     | unset    | Bucket region.                                                                           |
| `endpoint`   | unset    | Custom endpoint for non-AWS services, e.g. `https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`. |
| `public_url` | required | Public base URL of the bucket or its CDN; files are linked as `{public_url}/{key}`.      |
| `prefix`     | `""`     | Key prefix inside the bucket.                                                            |
| `path_style` | `false`  | Path-style requests (MinIO and most self-hosted services).                               |

```toml
[upload]
provider = { name = "s3", bucket = "media", region = "auto",
             endpoint = "https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com",
             public_url = "https://media.example.com" }
```

## `[webhooks]`

[Section titled “\[webhooks\]”](#webhooks)

| Key                      | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------ | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `allow_private_networks` | unset   | Allow webhook URLs on loopback, private and link-local addresses; also applies to deploy targets and the `[cdn]` webhook. Unset means no in `verdin start` (an admin could otherwise reach internal services) and yes in `verdin dev`. |
| `timeout_secs`           | `10`    | Time limit of each delivery.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `retention_days`         | `30`    | Days the delivery log is kept.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

See [Webhooks](/verdin/guides/integrations/webhooks/).

## `[history]`

[Section titled “\[history\]”](#history)

| Key            | Default | Description                                          |
| -------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `max_versions` | `50`    | Versions kept per document (older ones are removed). |

## `[email]`

[Section titled “\[email\]”](#email)

| Key        | Default                         | Description                                                      |
| ---------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `provider` | `"log"`                         | `log` (write emails to the log), `smtp`, `resend` or `postmark`. |
| `from`     | `"Verdin <no-reply@localhost>"` | Sender.                                                          |
| `reply_to` | unset                           | Reply-to address.                                                |

### `[email.smtp]`

[Section titled “\[email.smtp\]”](#emailsmtp)

| Key        | Default       | Description                                                              |
| ---------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `host`     | `"localhost"` | SMTP server.                                                             |
| `port`     | `587`         | SMTP port.                                                               |
| `username` | unset         | SMTP user; the password comes from `VERDIN_EMAIL_SMTP_PASSWORD`.         |
| `security` | `"starttls"`  | `starttls`, `tls` (implicit, usually port 465) or `none` (local relays). |

## `[plugins]`

[Section titled “\[plugins\]”](#plugins)

| Key        | Default     | Description                                                                             |
| ---------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `path`     | `"plugins"` | Directory of plugins (one sub-directory each), relative to the configuration file.      |
| `run_jobs` | `true`      | Run the plugins’ scheduled jobs on this instance (one instance when there are several). |

See [Plugins](/verdin/extending/plugins/).

## `[audit]`

[Section titled “\[audit\]”](#audit)

| Key              | Default | Description                      |
| ---------------- | ------- | -------------------------------- |
| `retention_days` | `90`    | Days audit log entries are kept. |

## `[digest]`

[Section titled “\[digest\]”](#digest)

| Key        | Default | Description                                                                     |
| ---------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `enabled`  | `true`  | Send the daily digest from this instance (one instance when there are several). |
| `hour_utc` | `8`     | Hour (UTC, 0–23) the daily digest of unseen changes goes out.                   |

## `[log]`

[Section titled “\[log\]”](#log)

| Key      | Default        | Description                                           |
| -------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `format` | `"pretty"`     | `pretty` or `json`.                                   |
| `level`  | unset (`info`) | Default filter; `RUST_LOG` takes precedence when set. |

## `[metrics]`

[Section titled “\[metrics\]”](#metrics)

| Key       | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `enabled` | `false` | Serve Prometheus metrics at `/_metrics`: HTTP requests by area (`api`, `admin_api`, `graphql`, `mcp`, `uploads`…), method and status class with latency histograms, pending webhook deliveries, open realtime streams, event bus traffic and uptime. |
| `token`   | unset   | Scrapes need `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. `VERDIN_METRICS_TOKEN` wins over it. Without a token, anyone who reaches the port can read the metrics.                                                                                                |

## `[telemetry]`

[Section titled “\[telemetry\]”](#telemetry)

Traces and error reports, both off by default and used only by `verdin start` and `verdin dev` (see [Monitoring](/verdin/deploy/monitoring/#traces-opentelemetry)).

| Key                  | Default                         | Description                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `enabled`            | `false`                         | Export OpenTelemetry traces of HTTP requests and their database queries over OTLP/HTTP (protobuf). `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true` turns it off.       |
| `endpoint`           | unset (`http://localhost:4318`) | Collector base URL; `/v1/traces` is appended. `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` (base URL) and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` (full URL) win. |
| `service_name`       | `"verdin"`                      | `service.name` of the traces. `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` wins.                                                                                         |
| `sample_ratio`       | `1.0`                           | Share of traces kept, from `0.0` to `1.0`. A request that carries a `traceparent` header follows the caller’s decision.                         |
| `sentry_dsn`         | unset                           | Report panics and 5xx responses to Sentry. `SENTRY_DSN` wins.                                                                                   |
| `sentry_environment` | unset                           | Sentry environment. `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT` wins; unset, `production` in `verdin start` and `development` in `verdin dev`.                         |

## `[ai]`

[Section titled “\[ai\]”](#ai)

AI actions in the admin (with the **AI** feature on in Settings → Features): translate an entry to another locale, write alt text for images, summarize text, suggest SEO metadata. They return suggestions; nothing is saved without the editor. The key is read from `VERDIN_AI_KEY` (local servers need none).

| Key          | Default                           | Description                                                              |
| ------------ | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `provider`   | `"none"`                          | `anthropic`, `openai` or `openai-compatible` (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM…). |
| `model`      | `claude-sonnet-5` for `anthropic` | The model; required for the other providers.                             |
| `base_url`   | the provider’s                    | Another endpoint, e.g. `http://localhost:11434/v1`.                      |
| `max_tokens` | `2048`                            | Longest answer.                                                          |

```toml
[ai]
provider = "anthropic"
```

Each admin may make 30 AI requests a minute. Content and images are sent to the provider: choose one your organization allows.

## `[cdn]`

[Section titled “\[cdn\]”](#cdn)

Purges CDN caches when content changes publicly. Content API responses are tagged `vd` and `vd-<singularName>` (`Cache-Tag` and `Surrogate-Key` headers).

| Key           | Default  | Description                                   |
| ------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `provider`    | `"none"` | `cloudflare`, `fastly` or `webhook`.          |
| `zone_id`     | unset    | Cloudflare zone (purge by tag).               |
| `service_id`  | unset    | Fastly service (purge by surrogate key).      |
| `url`         | unset    | `webhook`: receives `POST { "tags": [...] }`. |
| `debounce_ms` | `1000`   | Changes gathered before purging.              |

The API token is read from `VERDIN_CDN_TOKEN` (sent as a bearer token to webhooks).

## `[search]`

[Section titled “\[search\]”](#search)

| Key         | Default         | Description                                                                                 |
| ----------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `enabled`   | `false`         | Rank `_q` with a full-text index (Tantivy) instead of `$containsi`.                         |
| `dir`       | `"data/search"` | Index directory, relative to the project. Deleting it rebuilds the index on the next start. |
| `memory_mb` | `50`            | Indexing memory budget.                                                                     |

The index lives on the instance’s disk. With several instances, turn on the [event bus](#cluster) so that each index follows the writes of all of them.

## `[cluster]`

[Section titled “\[cluster\]”](#cluster)

The shared event bus, for several instances of one project (see [Running several instances](/verdin/deploy/scaling/#shared-event-bus)).

| Key                | Default                      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bus`              | `"none"`                     | `none`: realtime events, presence, cache invalidation and search updates stay in each instance. `database`: they reach every instance through the project’s database (`LISTEN/NOTIFY` on PostgreSQL, polling on MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite). |
| `poll_interval_ms` | `1000`                       | How often MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite read other instances’ events. PostgreSQL is woken by `NOTIFY` and uses this pace only while it cannot listen.                                                                                           |
| `instance_id`      | unset (random at each start) | This instance’s name on the bus and in the logs.                                                                                                                                                                                            |

```toml
[cluster]
bus = "database"
```

Set it on every instance, or with `VERDIN_CLUSTER__BUS=database`.

## Environment variables

[Section titled “Environment variables”](#environment-variables)

Besides the `VERDIN_<SECTION>__<KEY>` overrides, Verdin reads these variables:

| Variable                                                            | Description                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `VERDIN_CONFIG`                                                     | Path of the configuration file (same as `--config`).                                                                                                                              |
| `VERDIN_DATABASE_URL`                                               | Shorthand for `database.url`.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `VERDIN_ADMIN_JWT_SECRET`                                           | Signs admin session tokens. Required, at least 32 bytes; generate it with `verdin secrets`.                                                                                       |
| `VERDIN_TOKEN_PEPPER`                                               | Keyed hash for stored tokens. Required, at least 32 bytes; generate it with `verdin secrets`.                                                                                     |
| `VERDIN_ADMIN_PASSWORD`                                             | Password for `verdin admin create` and `verdin admin reset-password` (otherwise read from stdin); see the [command line reference](/verdin/reference/cli/).                       |
| `VERDIN_EMAIL_SMTP_PASSWORD`                                        | SMTP password.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `VERDIN_EMAIL_API_KEY`                                              | API key of the Resend and Postmark providers.                                                                                                                                     |
| `VERDIN_SSO_<ID>_SECRET`                                            | Client secret of an SSO provider; `<ID>` is the provider’s id in uppercase with `-` as `_` (see [Single sign-on](/verdin/guides/auth/sso/)).                                      |
| `VERDIN_OAUTH_<PROVIDER>_SECRET`                                    | Client secret of an end-user OAuth provider, named like the SSO ones (see [End users](/verdin/guides/auth/end-users/)).                                                           |
| `VERDIN_AI_KEY`                                                     | API key of the `[ai]` provider.                                                                                                                                                   |
| `VERDIN_CDN_TOKEN`                                                  | API token of the `[cdn]` provider.                                                                                                                                                |
| `VERDIN_IMAGE_SECRET`                                               | Signs image transformation URLs (see [`[upload.transforms]`](#uploadtransforms)).                                                                                                 |
| `VERDIN_METRICS_TOKEN`                                              | Bearer token for `/_metrics` scrapes when `[metrics].enabled`; wins over `[metrics].token`.                                                                                       |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` | Collector for [`[telemetry]`](#telemetry) traces; win over `[telemetry].endpoint`. The other standard `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` variables (headers, timeout, compression) apply too. |
| `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`, `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`                     | Resource of the exported traces; `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` wins over `[telemetry].service_name`.                                                                                        |
| `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED`                                                 | `true` turns trace export off even when `[telemetry].enabled`.                                                                                                                    |
| `SENTRY_DSN`, `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT`                                  | Sentry error reporting; win over `[telemetry].sentry_dsn` and `sentry_environment`.                                                                                               |
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`                        | Credentials of the S3 upload provider.                                                                                                                                            |
| `RUST_LOG`                                                          | Log filter; takes precedence over `[log].level`.                                                                                                                                  |

# Permissions reference

> Every admin permission and content API action Verdin checks, generated from the server's code.

This page lists every permission Verdin checks. It is generated from [`crates/verdin-auth/src/permissions.rs`](https://github.com/Verdin-CMS/verdin/blob/main/crates/verdin-auth/src/permissions.rs) on every build, so it matches the server. For how roles, tokens and the public role fit together, see [Permissions](/verdin/concepts/permissions/).

Verdin has two separate permission systems:

* **Admin permissions** decide what an admin user can do in the admin panel and the admin API. They belong to roles, edited in **Settings → Roles**; a user has the union of their roles’ permissions.
* **Content API actions** decide what a caller of `/api` and `/graphql` can do: anyone without a token (**Settings → Public access**), an API token (**Settings → API tokens**) or a signed-in end user (their role in **Settings → End users**).

## Admin permissions

[Section titled “Admin permissions”](#admin-permissions)

An admin permission is an action, plus, depending on the kind of action:

* **Content actions** take a subject: one content type (`api::article`) or all of them (`*`, **All content types**). They can be limited further:

  * to the documents the user created (the `is-creator` condition, shown as **Own**);
  * on `content.read`, `content.create` and `content.update`, to some fields (**Fields**). Other fields are hidden from reads and rejected on writes;
  * on localized types, to some locales.

* **Media library actions** take no subject. `is-creator` limits them to the user’s own files (**Own files**).

* **Settings actions** take no subject and no conditions: the user has them or not.

Super Admin is allowed everything by code and has no permission rows. Some operations are reserved to Super Admins whatever the permissions: managing Super Admin accounts, giving the Super Admin role, and switching single sign-on.

### Built-in roles

[Section titled “Built-in roles”](#built-in-roles)

| Role        | Permissions                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Super Admin | Everything.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Editor      | Every content action on all content types, every media library action, `deploy.trigger` and `site.manage`.                                                                                           |
| Author      | `content.read`, `content.create`, `content.update` and `content.delete` on their own entries (no publishing); `media.read` and `media.create`, `media.update` and `media.delete` on their own files. |

Existing installations receive the permissions added to the built-in roles in later versions once, on upgrade.

### Content

[Section titled “Content”](#content)

| Action            | Label in **Roles** | Allows                                                                                 |
| ----------------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `content.read`    | Read               | See entries of the type in the admin panel.                                            |
| `content.create`  | Create             | Create entries, clone them and import them.                                            |
| `content.update`  | Update             | Edit entries, restore versions from their history and move them between review stages. |
| `content.delete`  | Delete             | Delete entries.                                                                        |
| `content.publish` | Publish            | Publish and unpublish entries, discard drafts, and publish the entries of a release.   |

### Media library

[Section titled “Media library”](#media-library)

| Action         | Label in **Roles** | Allows                                                                                  |
| -------------- | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `media.read`   | Read files         | Browse the **Media library** and pick files in entries.                                 |
| `media.create` | Upload files       | Upload files (also from a URL) and create folders.                                      |
| `media.update` | Edit files         | Edit file details and replace files. Renaming and moving folders needs it on all files. |
| `media.delete` | Delete files       | Delete files. Deleting folders needs it on all files.                                   |

### Users and access

[Section titled “Users and access”](#users-and-access)

| Action            | Label in **Roles** | Allows                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `users.manage`    | Manage users       | Invite, edit, deactivate and delete admin users, and reset their second factors. Only a Super Admin can manage Super Admins or give that role. |
| `roles.manage`    | Manage roles       | Create, edit and delete admin roles, and edit **Public access** (what the content API allows without a token).                                 |
| `tokens.manage`   | Manage API tokens  | Create, regenerate and delete **API tokens**.                                                                                                  |
| `endusers.manage` | Manage end users   | Manage **End users**: their accounts and their roles on the content API.                                                                       |

### Content model and editing

[Section titled “Content model and editing”](#content-model-and-editing)

| Action           | Label in **Roles**      | Allows                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `schema.manage`  | Manage content types    | Use the **Content-type builder** (it edits schema files, so only in `verdin dev`).                                        |
| `locales.manage` | Manage locales          | Add, edit and remove locales in **Internationalization**.                                                                 |
| `views.manage`   | Configure entry editors | Configure the entry editor of each content type (field order, sizes, labels). Anyone who can read a type sees its layout. |

### Publishing workflows

[Section titled “Publishing workflows”](#publishing-workflows)

| Action             | Label in **Roles**      | Allows                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------ | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `releases.manage`  | Manage releases         | Create, edit, publish and delete **Releases**, and add entries to them.                                                         |
| `workflows.manage` | Manage review workflows | Create, edit and delete **Review workflows**, and move entries to any stage (others only reach the stages open to their roles). |

### Platform

[Section titled “Platform”](#platform)

| Action            | Label in **Roles** | Allows                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `features.manage` | Manage features    | Switch features on and off in **Features** and edit their settings, and send a test email. Switching single sign-on is reserved to Super Admins. |
| `webhooks.manage` | Manage webhooks    | Create, edit and delete **Webhooks**, rotate their secrets, trigger them and retry deliveries.                                                   |
| `plugins.manage`  | Manage plugins     | See installed **Plugins**, switch them on and off, edit their settings and read their logs.                                                      |
| `audit.read`      | Read audit logs    | Read the **Audit logs**.                                                                                                                         |

### Site and delivery

[Section titled “Site and delivery”](#site-and-delivery)

| Action           | Label in **Roles**                     | Allows                                                                                      |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `deploy.manage`  | Manage deploy targets and the CDN      | Manage deploy targets in **Deployments** and purge the CDN; includes triggering deploys.    |
| `deploy.trigger` | Trigger deploys                        | Trigger deploys of the configured targets.                                                  |
| `site.manage`    | Manage SEO, redirects, menus and forms | Manage SEO and sitemap settings, **Redirects**, **Menus**, **Forms** and their submissions. |

## Content API actions

[Section titled “Content API actions”](#content-api-actions)

The public role, API tokens with the **Custom** type and end-user roles grant these actions per content type. The media library (`plugin::upload`), the end-user accounts of `/api/users` (`plugin::users-permissions.user`) and the list of locales at `/api/i18n/locales` (`plugin::i18n.locale`) have rows of their own in the same grid. Everything is closed by default.

| Action       | Label       | Allows                                                                                        |
| ------------ | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `find`       | Find        | `GET /api/{pluralName}` (and single types’ `GET`), GraphQL list queries.                      |
| `findOne`    | Find one    | `GET /api/{pluralName}/{documentId}`, GraphQL single queries.                                 |
| `create`     | Create      | `POST`: create entries.                                                                       |
| `update`     | Update      | `PUT`: update entries.                                                                        |
| `delete`     | Delete      | `DELETE`: delete entries.                                                                     |
| `publish`    | Publish     | `POST /api/{pluralName}/{documentId}/actions/publish` (also `unpublish` and `discard-draft`). |
| `readDrafts` | Read drafts | Reading `?status=draft`.                                                                      |

`publish` and `readDrafts` do not apply to the media library and users rows. The locales row takes `find` only, as Strapi’s i18n plugin does. Reading drafts needs `readDrafts` on top of `find` or `findOne`.

### API token types

[Section titled “API token types”](#api-token-types)

| Type          | Label       | Allows                                          |
| ------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `read-only`   | Read-only   | `find` and `findOne` on every type (no drafts). |
| `full-access` | Full access | Every action on every type.                     |
| `custom`      | Custom      | Only the listed grants.                         |

Plugin routes and plugin GraphQL fields do their own access checks: the content API actions above do not apply to them (see [Plugin reference](/verdin/extending/plugin-reference/)).

# Installation

> Install the verdin binary with the install script, Homebrew, a .deb package, winget, cargo binstall or from source, or run the Docker image.

Verdin is one binary with the admin panel built in. Every release publishes it for Linux (x86-64 and ARM64, static musl builds), macOS (Intel and Apple silicon) and Windows (x86-64), with a `SHA256SUMS` file, on the [releases page](https://github.com/verdin-cms/verdin/releases). Pick whichever way of installing it suits your machine; they all install the same binary.

Check it with:

```sh
verdin --version
```

Then follow the [Quickstart](/verdin/start/quickstart/) from `verdin new`.

## Install script (Linux and macOS)

[Section titled “Install script (Linux and macOS)”](#install-script-linux-and-macos)

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/verdin-cms/verdin/main/install.sh | sh
```

The script detects the system and architecture, downloads the matching archive from the latest GitHub release, checks it against the release’s `SHA256SUMS` and installs `verdin` to `/usr/local/bin` when run as root, else to `~/.local/bin`. It needs `curl` or `wget`, `tar`, and `sha256sum`, `shasum` or `openssl`.

| Option              | Variable             | Default                                   |
| ------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `--version <X.Y.Z>` | `VERDIN_VERSION`     | The latest release                        |
| `--dir <directory>` | `VERDIN_INSTALL_DIR` | `/usr/local/bin` (root) or `~/.local/bin` |

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/verdin-cms/verdin/main/install.sh | sh -s -- --version 0.11.0 --dir /opt/verdin/bin
```

To read the script before running it, download it first: `curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/verdin-cms/verdin/main/install.sh`.

## Package managers

[Section titled “Package managers”](#package-managers)

* Homebrew

  On macOS and Linux:

  ```sh
  brew install verdin-cms/tap/verdin
  ```

  The formula installs the release binary (the musl build on Linux). `brew upgrade verdin` moves to the next release.

* Debian / Ubuntu

  Download the `.deb` for your architecture (`amd64` or `arm64`) from the release and install it:

  ```sh
  curl -fsSLO https://github.com/verdin-cms/verdin/releases/download/v0.11.0/verdin_0.11.0-1_amd64.deb
  sudo apt install ./verdin_0.11.0-1_amd64.deb
  ```

  The package adds a `verdin` system user, a systemd service (not enabled) and the configuration in `/etc/verdin/`. [Linux server](/verdin/deploy/linux-server/) walks through running it. There is no apt repository yet: upgrade by installing the next release’s `.deb`.

* winget

  On Windows:

  ```powershell
  winget install VerdinCMS.Verdin
  ```

  winget adds `verdin` to the `PATH` of new terminals. Without winget, download the `.zip` from the release and put `verdin.exe` somewhere on your `PATH`.

* cargo binstall

  With [cargo-binstall](https://github.com/cargo-bins/cargo-binstall), Cargo downloads the release binary instead of compiling it:

  ```sh
  cargo binstall --git https://github.com/verdin-cms/verdin verdin
  ```

## Docker

[Section titled “Docker”](#docker)

The image `ghcr.io/verdin-cms/verdin` runs the same binary on `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`:

```sh
docker run --rm ghcr.io/verdin-cms/verdin:0.11 --version
```

See [Docker](/verdin/deploy/docker/) for volumes, configuration and Compose files.

## From source

[Section titled “From source”](#from-source)

With Rust 1.95 or later and Node.js 24 (to build the admin panel):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/verdin-cms/verdin && cd verdin
(cd admin && npm ci && npm run build)
cargo install --locked --path crates/verdin --features embed-admin
```

Without `--features embed-admin` the binary has no admin panel, unless you point `[admin].assets_dir` at a built copy.

## Verify a download by hand

[Section titled “Verify a download by hand”](#verify-a-download-by-hand)

Each release has a `SHA256SUMS` file listing every archive and package:

```sh
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/verdin-cms/verdin/releases/download/v0.11.0/SHA256SUMS
sha256sum --check --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS     # macOS: shasum -a 256 --check --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS
```

# What is Verdin

> Verdin is an open source headless CMS written in Rust, with Strapi v5 compatible content APIs and an admin panel in one binary.

Verdin is an open source headless CMS written in Rust. You model content types, your editors write and publish in an admin panel, and your sites and apps read the content through a REST or GraphQL API. Verdin does not render pages: your frontend does.

It is a rewrite of [Strapi v5](https://strapi.io): the schema format and the content API have the same shape, so a Strapi project and its frontend can move over with few changes.

## Who it is for

[Section titled “Who it is for”](#who-it-is-for)

* **Developers building a site or app** who want a CMS they can run as one process, keep the content model in git, and read from any frontend: Astro, Next.js, a mobile app.
* **Teams on Strapi** who want the same API with a smaller footprint, or need features that Strapi reserves for paid plans. Verdin has no enterprise edition: SSO, audit logs, review workflows and releases are part of the open source project.
* **Editors**, who get drafts, publishing, history and previews in an admin panel available in 18 languages.

## What is in the box

[Section titled “What is in the box”](#what-is-in-the-box)

One executable, `verdin`, is the server, the command-line tool and the admin panel. There is no Node.js runtime and no `node_modules` in production.

| Area           | What you get                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Databases      | PostgreSQL 14+, MySQL 8.4+, MariaDB 10.11+ and SQLite, covered by the same test suite.                                                                                       |
| Content model  | Collection types, single types, components, dynamic zones, relations, media, rich text in Markdown or Strapi’s blocks format. The schema is JSON files in your project.      |
| Schema changes | Every change becomes a migration plan with a risk level and the exact SQL. Destructive steps only run when you allow them.                                                   |
| APIs           | REST under `/api` with Strapi v5 parameters (`filters`, `populate`, `sort`, `pagination`), an optional GraphQL endpoint, an OpenAPI document, and a typed TypeScript client. |
| Editing        | Draft and publish, localized content, content history, releases, review workflows, comments and tasks, live presence, preview and visual editing on your own site.           |
| Access         | Admin roles down to fields and locales, API tokens, public access grants, SSO with OpenID Connect, two-factor sign-in with passkeys, audit logs.                             |
| Site features  | Full-text search, sitemap, redirects, menus and forms, webhooks, realtime updates.                                                                                           |
| Extending      | WebAssembly plugins that hook into writes, add routes and jobs, and bring admin widgets and custom fields, limited to the capabilities they declare.                         |

## How it relates to Strapi v5

[Section titled “How it relates to Strapi v5”](#how-it-relates-to-strapi-v5)

**The same:**

* Schema files use Strapi’s format: `schema/content-types/<singularName>.json` and `schema/components/<category>/<name>.json`.
* The REST content API: routes, the flat response format with `documentId`, query parameters and operators, write semantics (a `POST` or `PUT` publishes unless you pass `?status=draft`), error bodies.
* The GraphQL schema is shaped like Strapi v5’s GraphQL plugin.
* End users (sign-up, sign-in, OAuth, roles) follow the `users-permissions` API.

**Different:**

* **Schema changes are planned migrations.** Verdin compares the schema files with the database and shows you the steps before it runs them. `verdin start` refuses to run while the database is behind the schema.
* **The content-type builder runs in development mode only.** In production the schema comes from your repository.
* **Plugins are WebAssembly, not JavaScript.** Strapi plugins, and custom controllers, services or lifecycle files in `src/`, do not run in Verdin.
* **The database is not shared with Strapi.** You bring a Strapi project over with `verdin import strapi`, which gives every document a new id.
* **A few extras over REST**: publish and unpublish actions (`POST /api/<route>/<documentId>/actions/publish`), and a populated component comes back whole, nested components included.

[Compatibility with Strapi](/verdin/migrate/compatibility/) lists the differences in detail.

## When not to use it

[Section titled “When not to use it”](#when-not-to-use-it)

* **You depend on Strapi plugins or custom server code in JavaScript.** Verdin cannot run them; you would rewrite them as WebAssembly plugins or move the logic elsewhere.
* **You need a stable 1.0.** Verdin is at 0.10: minor releases can still change configuration and behaviour. Read [Upgrading](/verdin/migrate/upgrading/) before each one.
* **You want the CMS to render your pages.** Verdin is headless; pair it with a frontend framework or a static site generator.
* **You want a managed service.** Verdin is self-hosted: you run the binary or the Docker image on your own infrastructure.

## Where to go next

[Section titled “Where to go next”](#where-to-go-next)

* [Quickstart](/verdin/start/quickstart/): run Verdin and read your first entry from the API.
* [Tutorial: a blog with Astro](/verdin/start/tutorial-astro/) or [with Next.js](/verdin/start/tutorial-nextjs/): build a frontend against the example blog.
* [Content model](/verdin/concepts/content-model/): content types, fields and how they are stored.
* [Importing a Strapi project](/verdin/migrate/from-strapi/): bring an existing project over.

# Project structure

> The files verdin new creates, the ones Verdin adds while it runs, and which of them belong in git.

A Verdin project is a directory with a configuration file and the schema. This page lists what `verdin new` creates, what the server adds while it runs, and what to commit.

## What `verdin new` creates

[Section titled “What verdin new creates”](#what-verdin-new-creates)

Terminal

```sh
verdin new my-site
```

* my-site/

  * verdin.toml project configuration

  * .env secrets and the database URL, readable by you only

  * .gitignore

  * schema/

    * content-types/ one JSON file per content type

      * …

    * components/ one folder per component category

      * …

  * data/ the SQLite database (only with `--database sqlite`)

    * …

The directory must not exist or must be empty. The project name in the database URL comes from the directory name, lowercased, with other characters replaced by `_` (`My Site` becomes `my_site`).

### `verdin.toml`

[Section titled “verdin.toml”](#verdintoml)

The configuration. The generated file sets the port, the content API prefix and page sizes, and the admin path:

verdin.toml

```toml
[server]
port = 1337
# public_url = "https://cms.example.com"


[api]
prefix = "/api"
default_page_size = 25
max_page_size = 100


[admin]
path = "/admin"
# secure_cookies = true
```

Every key has a default, so the file may be empty or missing. Unknown keys stop the server with an error. Any key can be overridden from the environment as `VERDIN_<SECTION>__<KEY>`, for example `VERDIN_SERVER__PORT=8080`. Commands read `verdin.toml` from the current directory; pass `-c <path>` or set `VERDIN_CONFIG` to use another file. Paths in the file, such as the schema or upload directories, are relative to the directory that contains it. All settings are in the [configuration reference](/verdin/reference/configuration/).

### `.env`

[Section titled “.env”](#env)

.env

```sh
# Local secrets: keep this file out of version control.
VERDIN_DATABASE_URL=sqlite://data/verdin.db
VERDIN_ADMIN_JWT_SECRET=…
VERDIN_TOKEN_PEPPER=…
```

`verdin new` fills in two random secrets and a database URL for the engine you chose with `--database`:

| `--database`       | Generated `VERDIN_DATABASE_URL`                     |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `sqlite` (default) | `sqlite://data/verdin.db`                           |
| `postgres`         | `postgres://verdin:change-me@localhost:5432/<name>` |
| `mysql`, `mariadb` | `mysql://verdin:change-me@localhost:3306/<name>`    |

Replace the user and password for PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB. Relative SQLite paths are resolved against the project directory, not the directory you run the command from.

Every command loads the `.env` next to `verdin.toml`; variables already set in the environment win. On Linux and macOS the file is created readable by its owner only. In production, set these variables in your platform’s secret store instead of shipping a `.env` file. The [Quickstart](/verdin/start/quickstart/#2-secrets) explains the two secrets.

### `schema/`

[Section titled “schema/”](#schema)

The content model, in Strapi’s schema format:

* `schema/content-types/<singularName>.json`, one file per collection or single type.
* `schema/components/<category>/<name>.json`, one file per component; the component’s uid is `<category>.<name>`.

The content-type builder writes these files in `verdin dev`, and you can edit them by hand: `verdin dev` reloads when they change. The schema of the example blog looks like this:

* schema/

  * content-types/

    * article.json
    * category.json
    * homepage.json single type
    * tag.json

  * components/

    * blocks/

      * hero.json `blocks.hero`
      * quote.json `blocks.quote`

    * shared/

      * seo.json `shared.seo`

The files are the source of truth: Verdin derives the database tables, validation, the REST and GraphQL APIs, the OpenAPI document, the TypeScript types and the admin forms from them. See [Content model](/verdin/concepts/content-model/) and [Schema migrations](/verdin/concepts/schema-migrations/). The schema directory is `[schema].path` in `verdin.toml`, `schema` by default.

## What appears when Verdin runs

[Section titled “What appears when Verdin runs”](#what-appears-when-verdin-runs)

* my-site/

  * verdin.toml

  * .env

  * schema/

    * …

  * data/

    * verdin.db SQLite database, with its `-wal` and `-shm` files

    * search/ full-text index, when `[search].enabled` is on

      * …

  * public/

    * uploads/ media library files, served at `/uploads`

      * …

  * .cache/

    * transforms/ resized images, rebuilt on demand

      * …

  * plugins/ WebAssembly plugins, one folder each (you create it)

    * …

  * strapi-id-map.json written by `verdin import strapi`

| Path                 | Written by                                              | Setting                         |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `data/verdin.db`     | The server, with SQLite                                 | `VERDIN_DATABASE_URL`           |
| `public/uploads/`    | Uploads with the local provider (the default)           | `[upload].provider`             |
| `.cache/transforms/` | Image transformations requested at `/uploads`           | `[upload.transforms].cache_dir` |
| `data/search/`       | The full-text index                                     | `[search].dir`                  |
| `plugins/`           | You: each plugin in its own folder                      | `[plugins].path`                |
| `strapi-id-map.json` | `verdin import strapi`: Strapi ids mapped to Verdin ids | —                               |

With PostgreSQL, MySQL or MariaDB there is no `data/verdin.db`: the content lives in the database server. With the S3 provider, media files live in the bucket and `public/uploads` stays empty.

## What goes in git

[Section titled “What goes in git”](#what-goes-in-git)

| Commit                                   | Keep out of git                         |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `verdin.toml`                            | `.env` (secrets)                        |
| `schema/` (content types and components) | `data/` (SQLite database, search index) |
| `plugins/`, if you use plugins           | `public/uploads/` (media)               |
| `.gitignore`                             | `.cache/`                               |

The generated `.gitignore` covers all of them:

.gitignore

```sh
.env
data/
*.db
*.db-*
.cache/
# Local media library ([upload.provider] dir).
public/uploads/
```

Projects created before 0.10 lack the `public/uploads/` line: add it.

Note

Content and media are data, not code. Back them up with `verdin export` or your database’s own tools rather than committing them; see [Backups](/verdin/deploy/backups/).

Commit the schema together with the code that depends on it, such as your frontend’s generated types. In production, deploy the committed schema and run `verdin start --migrate`: the content-type builder is off outside `verdin dev`, so the schema only changes through your repository.

# Quickstart

> Run Verdin with Docker or the binary, create the first admin, model a content type and read it from the API.

This page takes you from nothing to a first API response in about ten minutes: start Verdin, create the first admin, model a content type, open it to the public and read it over REST, GraphQL or the TypeScript client.

You need either [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) or a machine that can run the `verdin` binary (Linux, macOS or Windows on x86-64, Linux or macOS on ARM64).

## 1. Start Verdin

[Section titled “1. Start Verdin”](#1-start-verdin)

* Docker

  Generate the secrets once, then start the image in development mode:

  Terminal

  ```sh
  docker run --rm ghcr.io/verdin-cms/verdin secrets > verdin.env
  docker run -p 1337:1337 --env-file verdin.env -v verdin-data:/data ghcr.io/verdin-cms/verdin dev
  ```

  The `verdin-data` volume holds the SQLite database (`/data/verdin.db`), the uploaded media (`/data/uploads`) and, in `dev`, the schema files the content-type builder writes (`/data/schema`).

* Binary

  Install the binary (the admin panel is built in), for example with the install script on Linux and macOS:

  Terminal

  ```sh
  curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/verdin-cms/verdin/main/install.sh | sh
  ```

  Homebrew, a `.deb` package, winget, `cargo binstall` and the plain archives are in [Installation](/verdin/start/installation/).

  Scaffold a project and start it in development mode:

  Terminal

  ```sh
  verdin new my-site            # verdin.toml, schema/, .env with fresh secrets, SQLite
  cd my-site
  verdin dev
  ```

  `verdin new` takes `--database sqlite|postgres|mysql|mariadb` (SQLite by default) to choose the database the generated `.env` points at. For PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB, edit `VERDIN_DATABASE_URL` in `.env` to match your server before you run `verdin dev`. [Project structure](/verdin/start/project-structure/) describes every file it creates.

When the log shows `verdin listening`, the server answers on port 1337. The first start creates the database tables.

## 2. Secrets

[Section titled “2. Secrets”](#2-secrets)

Verdin needs two secrets, each at least 32 bytes long:

| Variable                  | What it protects                                                      |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `VERDIN_ADMIN_JWT_SECRET` | Signs admin sessions.                                                 |
| `VERDIN_TOKEN_PEPPER`     | Hashes API tokens and protects two-factor secrets and recovery codes. |

`verdin secrets` prints fresh values, and `verdin new` writes them into `.env`. Secrets come from the environment only, never from `verdin.toml`, and the server does not start without them. The `.env` file next to `verdin.toml` is loaded on start; variables already set in the environment win.

Caution

Generate the secrets once per installation and keep them. A new `VERDIN_ADMIN_JWT_SECRET` voids current sign-in tokens, open preview links and OAuth sign-ins in progress (the admin panel renews its session by itself); a new `VERDIN_TOKEN_PEPPER` invalidates every API token and every two-factor setup. Keep `.env` and `verdin.env` out of version control.

## 3. Create the first admin

[Section titled “3. Create the first admin”](#3-create-the-first-admin)

Open <http://localhost:1337/admin/>. While no administrator exists, the admin panel shows **Welcome to Verdin**: enter your name, email and a password of at least 8 characters, then select **Create account**. This first account is a Super Admin with every permission.

You can also create admins from the command line; see [Admin users from the command line](#admin-users-from-the-command-line).

## 4. Model a content type

[Section titled “4. Model a content type”](#4-model-a-content-type)

1. In the sidebar, open **Content-type builder** and select **New content type**.
2. Set **Display name** to `Article`. Verdin fills **Singular name (API id)** with `article` and **Plural name (route)** with `articles`; the route is the URL of the type in the API. Keep **Kind** on **Collection**.
3. Select **Add field**, choose **Short text**, name it `title`, and select **Done**.
4. Select **Save**. **Review the migration** lists the database steps with their SQL; select **Apply**.

Verdin writes the type to `schema/content-types/article.json` and creates its table. The builder is available in `verdin dev` only: in production the schema comes from your files. See [Content model](/verdin/concepts/content-model/) for field types and options.

Now add an entry: open **Article** under **Collections**, select **New entry**, fill in the title and select **Publish**. New types have **Draft & publish** on, so their entries stay drafts, invisible to the public API, until they are published.

## 5. Open it to the public

[Section titled “5. Open it to the public”](#5-open-it-to-the-public)

The content API is closed until you grant public permissions or create API tokens. Open **Settings → Public access**, allow **Find** and **Find one** for **Article**, and select **Save**.

To read without public access, create a token in **Settings → API tokens** and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. See [API tokens](/verdin/guides/auth/api-tokens/) and [Permissions](/verdin/concepts/permissions/).

## 6. Make a first request

[Section titled “6. Make a first request”](#6-make-a-first-request)

* REST

  Terminal

  ```sh
  curl localhost:1337/api/articles
  ```

  ```json
  {
    "data": [
      {
        "id": 2,
        "documentId": "01m3p88agn712n02wb8kkpe94p",
        "title": "Hello Verdin",
        "createdAt": "2026-09-29T09:34:39.637Z",
        "updatedAt": "2026-09-29T09:34:39.637Z",
        "publishedAt": "2026-09-29T09:34:39.637Z"
      }
    ],
    "meta": { "pagination": { "page": 1, "pageSize": 25, "pageCount": 1, "total": 1 } }
  }
  ```

  The response has the flat shape of Strapi v5. Filters, sorting, pagination and `populate` use the same query parameters; see the [REST API](/verdin/api/rest/).

* GraphQL

  Turn on **Settings → Features → GraphQL**. `POST /graphql` then serves a schema generated from your content types, with the same permissions as the REST API:

  Terminal

  ```sh
  curl localhost:1337/graphql -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -d '{"query":"{ articles { documentId title } }"}'
  ```

  ```json
  { "data": { "articles": [{ "documentId": "01m3p88agn712n02wb8kkpe94p", "title": "Hello Verdin" }] } }
  ```

  See the [GraphQL API](/verdin/api/graphql/).

* TypeScript

  Generate types from the schema and install the client in your frontend project:

  Terminal

  ```sh
  verdin types -o src/verdin-types.ts   # in the Verdin project
  npm install @verdin/client            # in the frontend project
  ```

  With Docker, the image can print the types from the schema in the volume: `docker run --rm -v verdin-data:/data ghcr.io/verdin-cms/verdin types > src/verdin-types.ts`.

  src/articles.ts

  ```ts
  import { createClient } from '@verdin/client';
  import type { VerdinSchema } from './verdin-types';


  const verdin = createClient<VerdinSchema>({ url: 'http://localhost:1337' });


  const { data } = await verdin.collection('articles').find({ sort: ['publishedAt:desc'] });
  console.log(data.map((article) => article.title));
  ```

  See [Typed client](/verdin/guides/frontend/typed-client/).

From here, the [Astro](/verdin/start/tutorial-astro/) and [Next.js](/verdin/start/tutorial-nextjs/) tutorials build a blog frontend on the same API.

## Development and production mode

[Section titled “Development and production mode”](#development-and-production-mode)

| Command                  | Use it for                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `verdin dev`             | Development: safe migrations apply automatically, the content-type builder can edit the schema files, and the server reloads when they change. |
| `verdin start`           | Production. It refuses to run while the database is behind the schema.                                                                         |
| `verdin start --migrate` | Production, applying pending safe migrations before starting. This is the Docker image’s default command.                                      |

Refresh cookies are `Secure` in `verdin start` and not in `verdin dev`, so sign-in to a `start` server needs HTTPS. To try `start` over plain HTTP, set `VERDIN_ADMIN__SECURE_COOKIES=false`.

In production, keep the schema in version control and mount it read-only. With Docker:

Terminal

```sh
docker run -p 1337:1337 --env-file verdin.env \
  -e VERDIN_DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:pass@db:5432/verdin \
  -v ./schema:/data/schema:ro ghcr.io/verdin-cms/verdin
```

The [production checklist](/verdin/deploy/production-checklist/) covers the rest.

## Schema and migrations

[Section titled “Schema and migrations”](#schema-and-migrations)

Content types live in `schema/content-types/<singularName>.json` and components in `schema/components/<category>/<name>.json`, in the Strapi format. When the files change, Verdin plans a migration:

Terminal

```sh
verdin schema check                      # validate every schema file
verdin migrate plan                      # steps, risk level and exact SQL
verdin migrate apply                     # safe steps only
verdin migrate apply --allow risky       # also type changes and new unique constraints
verdin migrate apply --allow destructive # also dropped columns and tables
verdin migrate apply --rename-column articles.title=headline --rename-table posts=articles
```

On MySQL and MariaDB, which have no transactional DDL, an interrupted migration resumes from the failed step on the next `migrate apply`. See [Schema migrations](/verdin/concepts/schema-migrations/).

## Admin users from the command line

[Section titled “Admin users from the command line”](#admin-users-from-the-command-line)

Terminal

```sh
verdin admin create --email other@example.com      # password from VERDIN_ADMIN_PASSWORD or stdin
verdin admin reset-password --email you@example.com
```

`admin create` creates a Super Admin. `reset-password` also unlocks the account and ends its sessions. Both need the database to be up to date with the schema.

## Other commands

[Section titled “Other commands”](#other-commands)

| Command                               | What it does                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `verdin types -o src/verdin-types.ts` | Writes TypeScript definitions of the content API (standard output without `-o`).          |
| `verdin import strapi <export>`       | Imports a Strapi project; see [Importing from Strapi](/verdin/migrate/from-strapi/).      |
| `verdin export <file.tar.gz>`         | Writes the schema, content and media to an archive; `verdin import verdin` reads it back. |
| `verdin version`                      | Prints the version.                                                                       |

Every command takes `-c, --config <path>` (default `verdin.toml`, or `VERDIN_CONFIG`). The [CLI reference](/verdin/reference/cli/) lists every command and flag, and the [configuration reference](/verdin/reference/configuration/) every setting.

## Health checks

[Section titled “Health checks”](#health-checks)

`GET /_health` answers while the process is up. `GET /_ready` also checks the database and answers 503 when it cannot reach it: point load balancers at it (see [Scaling](/verdin/deploy/scaling/)).

# Tutorial: a blog with Astro

> Build a small Astro blog on Verdin's example schema, with typed queries, article pages by slug, categories and an optional draft preview.

In this tutorial you build a static blog with [Astro](https://astro.build) that reads its content from Verdin: a home page that lists articles, one page per article at `/articles/<slug>/` with its category, and, optionally, a page that shows drafts from the admin’s preview link. You use the typed client `@verdin/client` with types generated from the schema.

Written for Astro 7.3 (`create-astro` 5.2) and Node.js 22.12 or later, with Verdin and `@verdin/client` 0.10. The [Next.js tutorial](/verdin/start/tutorial-nextjs/) builds the same blog with Next.js.

## Before you start

[Section titled “Before you start”](#before-you-start)

You need the `verdin` binary on your `PATH` (see the [Quickstart](/verdin/start/quickstart/)), Node.js and Git. You end up with two folders side by side: `cms`, the Verdin project, and `blog`, the Astro site.

## 1. Set up Verdin with the blog schema

[Section titled “1. Set up Verdin with the blog schema”](#1-set-up-verdin-with-the-blog-schema)

The repository’s [`examples/blog`](https://github.com/Verdin-CMS/verdin/tree/main/examples/blog) project models a blog: articles with a title, a `slug`, an excerpt, a Markdown `body`, a category and tags, plus a homepage single type and a few components.

1. Create a Verdin project and copy the example schema into it:

   Terminal

   ```sh
   git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Verdin-CMS/verdin.git
   verdin new cms
   cp verdin/examples/blog/schema/content-types/{article,category,tag,homepage}.json cms/schema/content-types/
   cp -r verdin/examples/blog/schema/components/* cms/schema/components/
   ```

2. Start it:

   Terminal

   ```sh
   cd cms
   verdin dev
   ```

   The first start creates the tables for the four content types.

3. Open <http://localhost:1337/admin/> and create the first admin.
